Core::Any::any_array_size.summary: Gets the size of the array held within the `any_array`, and returns it in the `size` port.

Core::Any::any_is_array.summary: Checks if the `any` contains an array. The `is_array` port is set to true if the any contains an array, and false otherwise.

Core::Any::get_any_array_values.summary: Gets the elements of the input `any_array` corresponding to the specified `indices` and returns them in `any_array_values`.

Core::Any::merge_any_arrays.summary: Merges an array of values of type `any`, each of which holds an array of the same concrete type, into a single `any` value that holds one array of that type. This can be useful when writing algorithms that manipulate arrays, without knowing the type of data held in the arrays.

Core::Any::resize_any_array.summary: Resizes the array held within the `any_array` input to the specified size.

Core::Array::all_true_in_array.summary: For an array of Booleans, returns whether all members are true. This is equivalent to a logical "and" over the array, and an empty array will return `true`.

Core::Array::any_true_in_array.summary: For an array of Booleans, returns whether any member is true. This is equivalent to a logical "or" over the array, and an empty array will return `false`.

Core::Array::array_bounds.summary: Returns the minimum and maximum values from the input array. For structs (vectors and matrices), the minimum and maximum are calculated member-by-member, and the result is the bounding box of the array elements.

Core::Array::array_is_empty.summary: Verify if an array is empty.

Core::Array::array_size.summary: Returns the number of elements in the array.

Core::Array::build_array.summary: Concatenates the inputs into a final array.

Core::Array::cumulative_sum_array.summary: Returns the array of partial sums of the input array. The first element of the output array is the first element of the input array, the second element is the sum of the first two, the third element is the sum of the first three, and so on.

Core::Array::empty_array.summary: Returns an empty array of the input type.

Core::Array::filter_array.summary: Filters an array using a boolean array to specify which elements to keep.

Core::Array::find_all_in_array.summary: Returns all `indices` of elements in an `array` that have values equal to `value`. This node works on arrays of all types that can be compared with `equal`.

Core::Array::find_all_true_in_array.summary: Computes an array whose elements are the indices of the input Boolean array's elements that are true. This is useful for computing a mapping when deleting elements from an array, or a group of arrays. Each element in the `indices` array will correspond to an index of an element to keep in the original array(s).

Core::Array::find_in_array.summary: Finds the index of the first occurrence of an item in an array, going from `start` to the end of the array.

Core::Array::find_in_sorted_array.summary: Finds the index of the first occurrence of an item in a sorted array, going from `start` to the end of the array. The `sort_array` node can be used to sort arrays. Finding many elements in a sorted array is faster than using `find_in_array` with an unsorted array.

Core::Array::first_in_array.summary: Returns the first element of an array. If the array is empty, a default value is returned.

Core::Array::flatten_nested_array.summary: Converts a nested n-dimensional array into a (n-1)-dimensional array. It does this flattening by concatenating the sub-arrays end to end.

Core::Array::get_array_indices.summary: Returns an array containing the indices of the input array. For example, if the input array has five elements, then the output is [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]

Core::Array::get_from_array.summary: Returns an element from the array.

Core::Array::intersect_arrays.summary: Returns the elements that are in both the `first_array` and `second_array` inputs. The order of elements in the `intersection` output is the same as `second_array`. If an element is duplicated in either input, the number of occurrences in `intersection` is the lower of the two counts.

Core::Array::last_in_array.summary: Returns the last element of an array. If the array is empty, a default value is returned.

Core::Array::prefix_sum.summary: Computes a prefix sum over the input array. A prefix sum is an array where every element is the sum of all elements up to that point in the input array.

Core::Array::remove_from_array.summary: Removes the elements with the specified indices from the input array.

Core::Array::reverse_array.summary: Produces an array where all elements are in the reverse order.

Core::Array::reverse_find_in_array.summary: Finds the index of the first occurrence of an item in an array, going from `start` to the beginning of the array.

Core::Array::set_in_array.summary: Sets the value of an element in the array.

Core::Array::shuffle_array.summary: Randomly shuffles the elements of the array.

Core::Array::slice_array.summary: Extracts a slice from an array.

Core::Array::small_slice.summary: Returns a slice of of the specified length from an array.

Core::Array::sort_array.summary: Sorts an array of numeric values using the natural ordering of the element type.

Core::Array::sort_array_and_remove_dupli.summary: Returns an array with duplicates removed - an array containing each unique value exactly once, sorted.

Core::Array::sort_array_with_indices.summary: Sorts an array and outputs the sorted array and an additional array of indices.

Core::Array::sum_array.summary: Adds all the elements of the input `array`, and returns the resulting `sum`.

Core::Constants::default_value.summary: Returns a default value of the input `type`. For numeric values, it is `zero`; for classes, it is a default constructed instance.

Core::Constants::e.summary: Returns the mathematical constant *e* (the base of the natural logarithms, approximately 2.71828) of the given type, such as `float` or `double`.

Core::Constants::golden_ratio.summary: Returns the golden ratio, which is often denoted by φ (Greek lowercase phi). The golden ratio is defined as (1 + sqrt(5))/2, and is approximately equal to 1.61803.

Core::Constants::identity.summary: Returns the multiplicative identity of the input type.

Core::Constants::numeric_max.summary: Returns the maximum absolute numeric value representable by the input type. For vectors and matrices, all members are set to the maximum value.

Core::Constants::numeric_min.summary: Returns the minimum absolute numeric value representable by the input type. For vectors and matrices, all members are set to the minimum value.

Core::Constants::numeric_small.summary: Returns the smallest positive non-zero number of the input type, such as `float` or `double`. For vectors and matrices, all members are set to the smallest value.

Core::Constants::one.summary: Returns the value 1 of the input type, such as `float` or `double`. For vectors and matrices, all members are set to 1.

Core::Constants::pi.summary: Returns the mathematical constant π (the ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter, approximately 3.14159) of the given type, such as `float` or `double`.

Core::Constants::tau.summary: Returns the value of τ (tau), the true circle constant, which is equal to 2π and is approximately 6.28319.

Core::Constants::zero.summary: Returns the value 0 of the input type, such as `float` or `double`. For vectors and matrices, all members are set to 0.

Core::Conversion::scalar_to_vector2.summary: Builds a vector2 from the component inputs.

Core::Conversion::scalar_to_vector3.summary: Builds a vector3 from the component inputs.

Core::Conversion::scalar_to_vector4.summary: Builds a vector4 from the component inputs.

Core::Conversion::vector2_to_scalar.summary: Splits a vector2 into its scalar components.

Core::Conversion::vector3_to_scalar.summary: Splits a vector3 into its scalar components.

Core::Conversion::vector3_to_vector4.summary: Builds a vector4 from a vector3 and a `w` component.

Core::Conversion::vector4_to_scalar.summary: Splits a vector4 into its scalar components.

Core::Conversion::vector4_to_vector3.summary: Splits a vector4 into a vector3 and a `w` component.

Core::FCurve::evaluate_fcurve.summary: Remaps the input `x` to the output `y` based on an editable function curve. This is useful for modulating effects using a custom profile, such as for falloffs and more.

Core::Fields::Internal::curl_noise_field.summary: A vector field that computes curl noise.

Core::Fields::Internal::fractal_block_no.summary: A scalar field whose value at any position is given by the sum of one or more layers of piecewise constant noise.

Core::Fields::Internal::fractal_disturba.summary: A vector field whose value at any position is given by the sum of one or more layers of piecewise constant noise in each component of the vector.

Core::Fields::Internal::fractal_noise_fi.summary: A scalar field whose value at any position is given by the sum of one or more layers of simplex noise.

Core::Fields::Internal::fractal_turbulen.summary: A vector field whose value at any position is given by the sum of one or more layers of curl noise.

Core::Fields::advect_field.summary: Advects a scalar or vector field along a velocity field for the length specified by the time step.

Core::Fields::closest_point_field.summary: Returns a vector field whose values are the closest point on the surface (0-level set) of the input signed distance field at any position.

Core::Fields::curl_field.summary: Returns a field whose values are the curl of the input vector field.

Core::Fields::curl_noise_field.summary: A vector field that computes curl noise.

Core::Fields::divergence_field.summary: Returns a field whose values are the divergence of the input vector field.

Core::Fields::fcurve_field.summary: Modulates a field using a function curve to remap the input field values to new ones.

Core::Fields::field_is_empty.summary: Returns whether the field is a null field (which always returns a zero value when evaluated). Use this to optimize the use of fields in the graph.

Core::Fields::fractal_block_noise_field.summary: A scalar field whose value at any position is given by the sum of one or more layers of piecewise constant noise.

Core::Fields::fractal_disturbance_field.summary: A vector field whose value at any position is given by the sum of one or more layers of piecewise constant noise in each component of the vector.

Core::Fields::fractal_noise_field.summary: A scalar field whose value at any position is given by the sum of one or more layers of simplex noise.

Core::Fields::fractal_turbulence_field.summary: A vector field whose value at any position is given by the sum of one or more layers of curl noise.

Core::Fields::gradient_field.summary: Returns a field whose values are the gradient of the input scalar field.

Core::Fields::mask_field.summary: Returns a field whose value is 1 where the input scalar field is positive, and 0 everywhere else.

Core::Fields::near_point_field.summary: Returns a field that follows the gradient of a scalar field toward 0 one or more times, and returns the new position. If the input is a signed distance field, this node is equivalent to `closest_point_field` but unlike that node, it can be used with any scalar field.

Core::Fields::plane_field.summary: A scalar field whose value at any position is the signed distance to the surface of a plane. Values above the plane in the direction of its normal are positive, and values below the plane are negative.

Core::Fields::position_field.summary: A vector field whose value at any position is simply the position itself.

Core::Fields::property_proxy_field.summary: Creates a property proxy field based on a property of a point-based geometry.

Core::Fields::rotate_field.summary: Returns a field whose values are rotated in space relative to the input field.

Core::Fields::sample_field.summary: Returns the value of a field at a position.

Core::Fields::sample_field_with_proxies.summary: Returns the array of values of a proxy field. Voxel proxy fields can be evaluated at positions, and property proxy fields can be evaluated at indices.

Core::Fields::scalar_field.summary: A scalar field whose value at any position is the input value. In addition to various Field nodes, scalar fields work with the following Core nodes: add, subtract, multiply, divide, negate, max, min, clamp, lerp, absolute_value, exponential, power, scalar_to_vector3.

Core::Fields::scale_field.summary: Returns a field whose values are scaled in space relative to the input field.

Core::Fields::simplex_noise_field.summary: A scalar field that computes simplex noise.

Core::Fields::smooth_field.summary: Returns a field whose values are the smoothed input scalar field.

Core::Fields::sphere_field.summary: A scalar field whose value at any position is the signed distance to the surface of a sphere. Values outside the sphere are positive, and values inside it are negative.

Core::Fields::superquadric_shape_field.summary: A scalar field representing ths shape as an implicit surface. The surface of the shape is at the zero level set. Note, unlike e.g. sphere_field this is not a signed distance field. I.e. the gradient is not necessarily one.

Core::Fields::switch_fields.summary: Returns one of two fields, depending on whether the `condition` field is positive.

Core::Fields::to_field.summary: Converts the input value to a scalar or vector field, depending on the type of the value. This provides a quick and convenient way to convert many types to a field, but not every type is supported.

Core::Fields::to_vector_field.summary: Promotes a scalar field to a vector field. Each component of the vector field is set to the value of the scalar field.

Core::Fields::transform_field.summary: Scales, rotates, and translates a field using a transform matrix.

Core::Fields::translate_field.summary: Returns a field whose values are offset in space relative to the input field.

Core::Fields::vector_field.summary: A vector field whose value at any position is the input vector. In addition to various Field nodes, vector fields work with the following Core nodes: add, subtract, multiply, divide, negate, max, min, clamp, lerp, absolute_value, power, cross, dot, length, length_squared, vector3_to_scalar.

Core::Fields::voxel_field.summary: Creates a voxel field from a volume geometry. The value of the field at any position is the value of the named property of the volume geometry, as interpolated between neighboring voxels.

Core::Fields::voxel_proxy_field.summary: Creates a voxel proxy field based on a property of a volume geometry. This is similar to creating an ordinary voxel field, but the difference is that you can supply the geometry later in the graph when you sample the proxy field using sample_field_with_proxies.

Core::Fields::warp_field.summary: Warps a scalar or vector field by a vector field.

Core::Graph::node_path.summary: Get the full path of this node_path node within the graph

Core::Internal::force_eval.summary: Passes the input through unchanged (similar to the "pass" node), but also forces the evaluation of the discard input.

Core::Internal::sleep.summary: Passes the input through unchanged (similar to the "pass" node), but "sleeps" for the queried amount of time before returning the output.

Core::Logging::Internal::log_message_imp.summary: Logs a message. Logging messages can be useful to debug the execution of Bifrost graphs.

Core::Logging::log_message.summary: Logs a message. Logging messages can be useful to debug the execution of Bifrost graphs.

Core::Logic::all_members_true.summary: Returns `true` if every component of a Boolean struct (vector or matrix) is `true`. If at least one component is `false`, it returns `false`. This is also called the logical conjunction.

Core::Logic::almost_equal.summary: Checks that two floating point values are equal to each other within `tolerance` in either relative or absolute terms (whichever is greater).

Core::Logic::and.summary: Returns `true` if both inputs are `true`. If at least one or both inputs are `false`, it returns `false`. This is also called the logical conjunction.

Core::Logic::any_members_true.summary: Returns `true` if at least one component of a Boolean struct (vector or matrix) is `true`. If all components are `false`, it returns `false`. This is also called the logical inclusive disjunction.

Core::Logic::equal.summary: Returns `true` if the first input is equal to the second one using the native ordering of the type.

Core::Logic::greater.summary: Returns `true` if the first input comes after the second one using the native ordering of the type.

Core::Logic::greater_or_equal.summary: Returns `true` if the first input comes after the second one using the native ordering of the type, or if they are equal.

Core::Logic::if.summary: This control flow node selects between two subgraphs based on the value of the condition input.

Core::Logic::less.summary: Returns `true` if the first input comes before the second one using the native ordering of the type.

Core::Logic::less_or_equal.summary: Returns `true` if the first input comes before the second one using the native ordering of the type, or if they are both equal.

Core::Logic::members_equal.summary: Returns a Boolean struct (vector or matrix) where each component is `true` if the corresponding component in the first input is equal to the same component in the second one.

Core::Logic::members_greater.summary: Returns a Boolean struct (vector or matrix) where each component is `true` if the corresponding component in the first input comes after the same component in the second one using the native ordering of the type.

Core::Logic::members_greater_or_equal.summary: Returns a Boolean struct (vector or matrix) where each component is `true` if the corresponding component in the first input comes after the same component in the second one using the native ordering of the type, or if they are both equal.

Core::Logic::members_if.summary: Returns a struct (vector or matrix) where the members are selected from two other structs based on a Boolean struct.

Core::Logic::members_less.summary: Returns a Boolean struct (vector or matrix) where each component is `true` if the corresponding component in the first input comes before the same component in the second one using the native ordering of the type.

Core::Logic::members_less_or_equal.summary: Returns a Boolean struct (vector or matrix) where each component is `true` if the corresponding component in the first input comes before the same component in the second one using the native ordering of the type, or if they are both equal.

Core::Logic::members_not_equal.summary: Returns a Boolean struct (vector or matrix) where each component is `true` if the corresponding component in the first input is not equal to the same component in the second one using the native ordering of the type.

Core::Logic::not.summary: Negates the truth value of the input.

Core::Logic::not_equal.summary: Returns `true` if the first input is not equal to the second one using the native ordering of the type.

Core::Logic::or.summary: Returns `true` if at least one of the inputs is `true`. If both inputs are `false`, it returns `false`. This is also called the logical inclusive disjunction.

Core::Logic::xor.summary: Returns `true` if one but not both of the inputs is `true`. If both inputs are `true` or both are `false`, it returns `false`. This is also called the logical exclusive disjunction.

Core::Math::SRT_to_matrix.summary: Constructs a transformation matrix from basic shear, scale, rotation, and translation components.

Core::Math::absolute_value.summary: Returns the absolute value of the input.

Core::Math::acos.summary: Returns the trigonometric arccosine of the input.

Core::Math::acos_hyperbolic.summary: Returns the inverse hyperbolic cosine of the input.

Core::Math::angle_around_axis.summary: Calculates the signed angle of a rotation around a given axis.

Core::Math::asin.summary: Returns the trigonometric arcsine of the input.

Core::Math::asin_hyperbolic.summary: Returns the inverse hyperbolic sine of the input.

Core::Math::atan.summary: Returns the trigonometric arctangent of the input.

Core::Math::atan_2D.summary: Computes the arctangent of y/x using the signs of arguments to determine the correct quadrant.

Core::Math::atan_hyperbolic.summary: Returns the inverse hyperbolic tangent of the input.

Core::Math::axis_angle_to_quaternion.summary: Converts a rotation about an axis to the corresponding quaternion representation.

Core::Math::bitwise_and.summary: Computes the bitwise logical conjunction of two integers.

Core::Math::bitwise_not.summary: Computes the bitwise negation of an integer.

Core::Math::bitwise_or.summary: Computes the bitwise logical inclusive disjunction of two integers.

Core::Math::bitwise_shift_left.summary: Shifts the bit pattern of the input integer `second` places to the left by padding with 0 and discarding the high bits that do not fit in the output integer.

Core::Math::bitwise_shift_left_circular.summary: Shifts the bit pattern of the input integer `second` places to the left. For every shift, the most significant bit falling out of integer range is copied to the least significant bit position.

Core::Math::bitwise_shift_right.summary: Shifts the bit pattern of the input integer `second` places to the right by padding with the value of the most significant bit and discarding the low bits. Negative values stay negative.

Core::Math::bitwise_shift_right_circular.summary: Shifts the bit pattern of the input integer `second` places to the right. For every shift, the least significant bit falling out of integer range is copied to the most significant bit position.

Core::Math::bitwise_xor.summary: Computes the bitwise logical exclusive disjunction of two integers.

Core::Math::change_range.summary: Remaps one or more `value` from one range to another.

Core::Math::clamp.summary: Clamps a value to specific bounds.

Core::Math::copy_sign.summary: Makes a number positive or negative based on the sign of the `sign` input.

Core::Math::cos.summary: Returns the trigonometric cosine of the input. On a right-angled triangle, this is the ratio of the length of the adjacent side divided by the length of the hypotenuse.

Core::Math::cos_hyperbolic.summary: Returns the hyperbolic cosine of the input.

Core::Math::cross.summary: Computes the cross product of two 3D vectors.

Core::Math::cube_root.summary: Computes the cube root of the input.

Core::Math::decrement.summary: Subtracts one (or another integer) from `value`. `by` allows you to specify the value to subtract.

Core::Math::direction_and_length.summary: Returns the direction and length of a vector.

Core::Math::distance.summary: Calculates the distance between two positions.

Core::Math::distance_float_ULP.summary: Computes exactly how many representable floating point numbers can exist between the two input values.

Core::Math::dot.summary: Computes the dot product of two vectors.

Core::Math::equivalent_float_ULP.summary: Checks if two floating point numbers are equivalent by calculating exactly how many representable floating point numbers can exist between the two values.

Core::Math::equivalent_float_epsilon.summary: Checks that two floating point values are equal to each other within a specific tolerance.

Core::Math::euler_to_quaternion.summary: Converts a vector3 of Euler angles into the corresponding quaternion. Since rotations are not commutative, the `order` of application must be specified.

Core::Math::euler_to_rotation_vector.summary: Converts a vector3 of Euler angles into the corresponding rotation vector. The order of the rotations assumed is XYZ.

Core::Math::find_orthogonal_vectors.summary: Returns two vectors at 90 degrees to each other and to the input vector.

Core::Math::get_from_interpolated_array.summary: Interpolates (blends) an incoming array by a float or array of floats, with the ability to slice the incoming array and interpolate the resulting slice.

Core::Math::get_member.summary: Returns an element from a vector or matrix type.

Core::Math::half_of.summary: Divides a `value` by two and returns the `half_value`.

Core::Math::hash_float.summary: Hash a floating point value to an integral value.

Core::Math::increment.summary: Adds one (or another integer) to `value`. `by` allows you to specify the value to add.

Core::Math::index_to_fraction.summary: converts an index in a range into a fraction between `0.0` to `1.0`. This is commonly used in loops to get a normalized value from the first to the last iteration.

Core::Math::interpolate_transform_matrix.summary: Interpolate between the shear, scale, quaternion, and translation components of two decomposed 4x4 transform matrices.

Core::Math::inverse_matrix.summary: Computes the inverse of a matrix.

Core::Math::length.summary: Returns the length of a vector.

Core::Math::length_squared.summary: Returns the square of the length of a vector. This is faster than `length` because it avoids a costly square root computation. It can be used to compare lengths when you are only concerned with which of two vectors is longer, and not what their actual lengths are.

Core::Math::lerp.summary: Computes the linear interpolation between two values.

Core::Math::linear_interpolate.summary: Computes the linear interpolation between two values.

Core::Math::linear_interpolate_array.summary: Creates an array whose values are evenly interpolated between two given values.

Core::Math::linear_interpolate_normalize.summary: Computes the linear interpolation between two vectors and normalizes the result.

Core::Math::matrix_determinant.summary: Returns the determinant of the matrix.

Core::Math::matrix_is_identity.summary: Checks if a matrix is identity or not.

Core::Math::matrix_is_orthonormal.summary: Checks if a matrix is orthonormal, meaning that it has no shear and the local X, Y, and Z axes are normalized and orthogonal to one another. A matrix is orthonormal if its determinant is equal to `1.0` or `-1.0`.

Core::Math::matrix_is_singular.summary: Checks if a matrix is singular, meaning that it cannot be inverted. A matrix is singular if its determinant is equal to `0.0`.

Core::Math::matrix_to_SRT.summary: Decomposes a transform matrix into its constituent shear, scale, rotation, and translation.

Core::Math::matrix_to_quaternion.summary: Returns a rotation expressed in quaternion form.

Core::Math::modulo.summary: Computes the remainder of the division operation `value/divisor`.

Core::Math::negate.summary: Changes the sign of the input value.

Core::Math::normal_and_tangent_to_orient.summary: Converts two vectors to an orientation. This is similar to an aim constraint, where one functions as an "aim" and the other as an "up" vector.

Core::Math::normalize.summary: Normalizes a vector by dividing each component by the original length.

Core::Math::project_vector.summary: Projects one vector onto another, and returns both the parallel and orthogonal components.

Core::Math::quaternion_conjugate.summary: Computes the conjugate of a quaternion.

Core::Math::quaternion_slerp.summary: Returns a spherical linear interpolation between two quaternions.

Core::Math::quaternion_to_axis_angle.summary: Returns the rotation expressed as a rotation around an axis.

Core::Math::quaternion_to_euler.summary: Returns the rotation expressed as a vector3 of Euler angles.

Core::Math::quaternion_to_matrix.summary: Returns a rotation expressed in matrix form.

Core::Math::quaternion_to_rotation_vecto.summary: Returns the rotation expressed as a rotation vector, where the vector direction is the rotation axis and the vector length the angle in radians.

Core::Math::remainder.summary: Computes the floating point remainder of `first` divided by `second`.

Core::Math::resize_vector.summary: Modifies the length of a vector.

Core::Math::rotate_by_quaternion.summary: Applies a rotation expressed as a quaternion to a vector.

Core::Math::rotate_vector_by_matrix.summary: Rotates a vector using the decomposed quaternion of a 3x3 rotation matrix or a 4x4 transform matrix.

Core::Math::rotation_around_position_to_.summary: Creates a 4x4 transform matrix representing a rotation around a position.

Core::Math::rotation_between_vectors.summary: Give two vectors, this generates the rotation between them. More precisely, this computes the quaternion corresponding to the rotation along the shortest arc that aligns the vector `from` with `to`.

Core::Math::rotation_vector_to_quaternio.summary: Converts a rotation vector to the corresponding quaternion representation.

Core::Math::round_to_ceiling.summary: Rounds a floating point value to the smallest integer greater than the input.

Core::Math::round_to_floor.summary: Rounds a floating point value to the largest integer less than the input.

Core::Math::round_to_nearest.summary: Rounds the floating point value to the nearest integer. This is also known as banker's rounding.

Core::Math::set_matrix_translation.summary: Replaces the translation component of a 4×4 transformation matrix with a new translation value.

Core::Math::sin.summary: Returns the trigonometric sine of the input. On a right-angled triangle, this is the ratio of the length of the opposite side divided by the length of the hypotenuse.

Core::Math::sin_hyperbolic.summary: Returns the hyperbolic sine of the input.

Core::Math::split_fraction.summary: Decomposes a floating point `value` into integral and fractional parts, each having the same type and sign as `value`.

Core::Math::square_root.summary: Computes the square root of the input value.

Core::Math::tan.summary: Returns the trigonometric tangent of the input. On a right-angled triangle, this is the ratio of the length of the opposite side divided by the length of the adjacent side.

Core::Math::tan_hyperbolic.summary: Returns the hyperbolic tangent of the input.

Core::Math::transform_to_rotation_matrix.summary: Converts a 4x4 transform matrix to a 3x3 normalized rotation matrix.

Core::Math::transform_vector.summary: Transforms a vector using various transformation methods.

Core::Math::transform_vector_as_directio.summary: Transform a vector interpreted as a direction vector, and transform it so that the vector is affected by the shearing, scaling, and orientation of a transform.

Core::Math::transform_vector_as_normal.summary: Transform a vector interpreted as a normal vector, such that the transformed vector stays perpendicular to a surface even when scaled or sheared. This is done by transforming it by the inverse-transpose (adjoint) of the normalized 3x3 rotation matrix component of a transform.

Core::Math::transform_vector_as_position.summary: Transform a vector interpreted as a position, fully affected by a transform.

Core::Math::truncate.summary: Computes the nearest integer not greater in magnitude than `value`.

Core::Math::twice_of.summary: Multiplies a `value` by two and returns the `double_value`.

Core::Math::within_bounds.summary: Tests whether a value is within certain bounds or not.

Core::Object::Internal::add_required_fre.summary: Adds free memory required by operations not using the memory pools.

Core::Object::Internal::clear_number_of_.summary: Clears stats about the number of copies.

Core::Object::Internal::disable_copies_t.summary: Disables tracking of copies of bif components.

Core::Object::Internal::enable_copies_tr.summary: Enables tracking of copies of bif components.

Core::Object::Internal::number_of_active.summary: The number of total active copies (copies that have not yet been freed).
The number of total active copies with a given name (copies that have not yet been freed).

Core::Object::Internal::number_of_copies.summary: The total number of copies registered (active and inactive).

The output arrays are structured using the "offset" array pattern often found in other places in Bifrost. See below for more details.

Geometry::Internal::hash_object.summary: This node hashes a Bifrost object.

Geometry::Internal::hash_points.summary: This node hashes point geometry (points, meshes, splines).

Geometry::Internal::insert_range_geo_pro.summary: Inserts a range geo property into a data geo property's target chain. This effectively makes a geo property indexed.

Geometry::Internal::mesh_components.summary: Outputs an array of strings that contain the canonical geo property names of mesh components (`point_component`, `face_vertex_component` and `face_component`).

Geometry::Internal::mesh_cube.summary: Populate an object with the properties of a mesh cube.

Geometry::Internal::mesh_plane.summary: Populate an object with the properties of a mesh plane.

Geometry::Internal::mesh_sphere.summary: Populate an object with the properties of a mesh sphere.

Geometry::Internal::sample_volume_proper.summary: Sample a value from a volume geometry.

Geometry::Internal::set_in_place_geo_pro.summary: Set a property on a volume object. If the property exists then the value is replaced else the property is added to the object. This operation is done in place, i.e. do not deep copy even when the object is shared between many instances.

Geometry::Internal::strand_components.summary: Outputs an array of strings that contain the canonical geo property names of the components of strand objects (`point_component` and `strand_component`).

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::find_highest_w.summary: For each target element, find the source ancestor with the highest weight from an offset-based weight array structure.

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::get_face_edge_.summary: Get the face vertex indices that correspond to the start and end points of the specified `face_edge`. Note that face edges are directed. The start point is the face vertex with the smaller face vertex index and the end vertex is the face vertex with the larger face vertex index. Note that if the start face vertex is the last face vertex in the face, the end face vertex will be the first face ve...
Gets the face edge that corresponds to the face that is adjacent to the specified `face_edge`.
Get the vertex indices of the specified `face_edge`. Note that face edges are directed from the lower face vertex index to the higher one.

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::get_next_face_.summary: Gets the next face edge in the corresponding face. The next face edge is the face edge that follows the specified one, when the face edges are traversed in a counter-clockwise order along the face. The first vertex of the `next_face_edge` is the second vertex of `face_edge`.

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::get_prev_face_.summary: Gets the previous face edge in the corresponding face. The previous face edge is the face edge that precedes the specified one, when the face edges are traversed in a counter-clockwise order along the face. The first vertex of the `face_edge` is the second vertex of `prev_face_edge`.

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::is_face_edge_c.summary: Determine if the specified `face_edge` is consistent.

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::is_face_edge_m.summary: Determine if the specified face edge is manifold. A face edge is manifold if it is open, or adjacent to at most one other face edge.

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::is_face_edge_o.summary: Determine if the specified face edge is open. An open face edge is one that is not adjacent to another face edge. Also known as a border edge.

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::normal_indexin.summary: Computes new face vertex normal indexing using an angle threshold. When the angle between adjacent faces exceeds the threshold the faces will be assigned their own normals along the shared edge. Visually this will give the appearance of a hardened edge. When the angle between adjacent faces is less than the threshold the faces will be assigned the same normals along the shared edge. Visually th...

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::remove_mesh_sl.summary: Removes narrow triangles from a triangle mesh.

Geometry::Mesh::Internal::update_fv_indi.summary: This node updates the normal indexing for a mesh, based on the angle between adjacent faces. When the angle exceeds the given threshold, the normals for the adjacent faces will be separated. When the angle is below the threshold, the faces will share a single normal.

Geometry::Mesh::compute_mesh_rigid_veloc.summary: Computes the best fit rigid velocity of the input mesh, i.e. the linear and angular velocity that best fits the `point_velocity`.

Geometry::Mesh::compute_mesh_surface_are.summary: Calculates the surface area of the given mesh.

Geometry::Mesh::compute_mesh_volume.summary: Computes the signed volume of the input mesh. The mesh is assumed to be a closed, watertight mesh whose faces all have a consistent winding order.

Geometry::Mesh::construct_mesh.summary: Creates a mesh geometry with only the properties that are required for a valid mesh structure.

Geometry::Mesh::face_group_to_points.summary: Finds the points that are referenced by the specified group of faces. The points are classified as interior or border points. An interior point is one that is completly surrounded by faces in the input `faces` group, and is not on a border of the input mesh. A border point is one that is on the boundary of the faces in the input `faces` group : it means it is not surrounded by selected faces, o...

Geometry::Mesh::faces_to_points.summary: Returns an array of points of the input mesh that are referenced by the faces in the input array.

Geometry::Mesh::filter_meshes.summary: Returns only the meshes from the input array of objects.

Geometry::Mesh::find_face_orientations.summary: This is used to detect faces with inconsistent winding orders.

Geometry::Mesh::find_mesh_islands.summary: Finds the islands of a mesh. An island is a group of faces where each face in the group is adjacent to other faces in the same group. A face cannot be a part of more than one island.

Geometry::Mesh::get_mesh_UVs.summary: Get the mesh's UV coordinates and corresponding face vertex indices.

Geometry::Mesh::get_mesh_structure.summary: Gets the canonical data for a mesh geometry (the point, face-vertex, and face data arrays and counts).

Geometry::Mesh::points_to_faces.summary: Returns an array of faces of a mesh that reference an input array of points.

Geometry::Mesh::sample_mesh_UVs.summary: Returns the value of a property at locations on a geometry. Values can be interpolated from the closest geometric components.

Geometry::Mesh::set_mesh_UVs.summary: Sets UV coordinate data into a mesh.

Geometry::Mesh::smooth_mesh.summary: This node smoothes a Bifrost mesh.

Geometry::Mesh::soften_harden_edges.summary: Soften/harden edges on a mesh based on the angle between faces. If the angle between adjacent faces exceeds the angle threshold, the edge between the faces will be hardened. Otherwise the edge between the faces will be softened.

Geometry::Mesh::sqrt3_subdivide_mesh.summary: This node subdivides a mesh using Leif Kobbelt's sqrt(3) subdivision algorithm from SIGGRAPH 2000.

Geometry::Mesh::triangulate_mesh.summary: Triangulates a Bifrost mesh. No new points are inserted. Face and face-vertex properties are copied to the new mesh.

Geometry::Mesh::update_face_centers.summary: Update the face centers on a mesh. A face's center point is the weighted average of its corner points.

Geometry::Mesh::update_face_normals.summary: Update the face normals on a mesh. A face's normal is the summed total of the normals of the triangles of the face.

Geometry::Mesh::update_face_tangent.summary: Tangents come in two flavours, `face_tangent` is the calculated tangent per face, computed from topology. `face_vertex_tangent` are the tangents of the verticies that make up the face, computed from UVs.

Geometry::Mesh::update_face_vertex_norma.summary: Update the normals on a mesh using the existing face vertex normal indexing. The existing indexing determines which edges appear as hard edges in the mesh. This compound will preserve the existing hardness. If face vertex normals don't exist on the mesh, this compound will create trivial face vertex normals where every edge is soft.

Geometry::Mesh::update_mesh_adjacency.summary: Builds the adjacency structures for a mesh.

Geometry::Mesh::update_mesh_normals.summary: Recalculates the `point_normal` property on a `mesh`. These are computed as the mean of the vertex's adjacent face normals.

Geometry::Mesh::update_point_neighbors.summary: Returns the neighbors of each point in a mesh based on edge connectivity.

Geometry::Mesh::validate_mesh.summary: Validate that the given object adheres to the mesh schema and that it contains valid data.

Geometry::Points::construct_points.summary: Constructs a `points` geometry - creating a `points` from raw data in the graph. This creates a minimal object, it does not set `point_size`, `point_orientation`, or any other optional properties.

Geometry::Points::filter_points.summary: Returns only the point objects (like particle systems) from the input array of objects. Note that other types of geometric objects that have points (such as meshes and strands) are not returned.

Geometry::Points::get_bounding_box.summary: Gets the world-aligned bounding box of the input point-based geometry or array of points.

Geometry::Points::get_points_structure.summary: Gets the canonical data of a points geometry (the point_positions array and the point count).

Geometry::Points::validate_points.summary: Validate that the given object adheres to the points schema and that it contains valid data.

Geometry::Properties::Internal::get_geo_.summary: Gets the geo property data as Any values. This is useful for algorithms that manipulate geo properties without knowing their data type.

Geometry::Properties::Internal::get_prop.summary: Get an array of properties and corresponding property names to transfer.

Geometry::Properties::Internal::set_comp.summary: Sets the number of elements for the specified `component`. Note that geo properties in the `geometry` that target the modified `component` will not be updated. Use the property transfer nodes to process related geo properties.

Geometry::Properties::copy_properties.summary: Copies properties from source objects to a target object.

Geometry::Properties::erase_component_pr.summary: Erases geo properties that target a component of a geometric object.

Geometry::Properties::erase_geo_properti.summary: Erases geo properties from the input geometry.

Geometry::Properties::extract_geo_proper.summary: Extracts the `data` array of the specified geometry property, such as the `point_size` property on points.

Extracts the `data` array of the specified geometry property, such as the `point_size` property on points. This is different from `extract_geo_property` because it also returns whether the property exists on the object.

Geometry::Properties::extract_point_norm.summary: Extract the array of point normals from a point geometry, such as particles, strands or meshes.

Geometry::Properties::extract_point_posi.summary: Extract the array of point positions from a point geometry, such as particles, strands or meshes.

Geometry::Properties::extract_point_velo.summary: Extract the array of point velocities from a point geometry, such as particles, strands or meshes.

Geometry::Properties::get_filtered_voxel.summary: Returns the voxel positions of a volume based on a `float` property, filtered by a threshold.  This returns an empty array if no property is specified, or if the property doesn't exist on the volume.

Geometry::Properties::get_geo_component_.summary: Returns the number of components in a geometric object, such as the number of points in a mesh.

Returns an array containing the indices of a component in a geometric object. For example, if the input geometry is a mesh with 4 faces and we want the `face_component` indices, then the output is [0, 1, 2, 3]

Geometry::Properties::get_geo_properties.summary: Get geo properties and their corresponding names from an expression.

Geometry::Properties::get_geo_property.summary: Returns the array of values of a property on the components of a geometric object, such as the `point_size` values of points.

Geometry::Properties::get_geo_property_c.summary: Returns the array of values of a property on the components of a geometric object, such as the `point_size` values of points. This is different from `get_geo_property` because it also returns whether the property exists on the object.

Geometry::Properties::get_geo_property_o.summary: Returns the array of values of a property on the components of a geometric object, such as the `point_size` values of points.

Geometry::Properties::get_indexed_geo_pr.summary: Returns the array of values of a property on the components of a geometric object, such as the `face_vertex_normals` of a mesh. Also returns the corresponding indices for the geo property.

Geometry::Properties::get_point_count.summary: Gets the number of points in a geometric object. This works for any object with points, including points objects like particle systems, as well as meshes, instances, and others.

Geometry::Properties::get_point_normal.summary: Returns the array of point normals for a mesh.

Geometry::Properties::get_point_position.summary: Returns the array of point positions for a geometric object. This works for any object with points, including points objects like particle systems, as well as meshes, instances, and others.

Geometry::Properties::get_point_velocity.summary: Returns the array of point velocities for a geometric object. This works for any object with points, including points objects like particle systems, as well as meshes, instances, and others.

Geometry::Properties::get_property_names.summary: Get the names of properties in the given object that match the given expression.

Geometry::Properties::get_voxel_fog_dens.summary: Returns the `voxel_fog_density` values of a volume if that property exists.

Geometry::Properties::get_voxel_position.summary: Returns the `voxel_positions` values of a volume if that property exists.

Geometry::Properties::get_voxel_signed_d.summary: Returns the `voxel_signed_distance` values of a volume if that property exists.

Geometry::Properties::get_voxel_velocity.summary: Returns the `voxel_velocity` values of a volume if that property exists.

Geometry::Properties::points_to_transfor.summary: Combines `point_position`, `point_orientation`, `point_scale` and `point_size` into a transform matrix. The resulting matrix is the matrix that would get applied to instances that are placed on these points.

Geometry::Properties::set_geo_property.summary: Creates and initializes a property that targets components such as points on a geometric object.

Geometry::Properties::set_geo_property_d.summary: Sets the data values of a an existing geometric property. For example, if `point_size` exists on the input object, you can use this node to change the sizes per point.

Geometry::Properties::set_indexed_geo_pr.summary: Creates and initializes an indexed property that targets components such as points on a geometric object.

Geometry::Properties::set_point_normal.summary: Sets the `point_normal` property to the values of the array.

Geometry::Properties::set_point_position.summary: Sets the `point_position` property to the values of the array.

Geometry::Properties::set_point_shape.summary: Sets the shape used for displaying and rendering points, such as from a particle system.

Geometry::Properties::set_point_velocity.summary: Sets the `point_velocity` property to the values of the array.

Geometry::Properties::transfer_propertie.summary: Transfer geo properties from multiple source geometries to a single target geometry. This is useful when building a new geometry object from many existing ones, and still retaining the existing geometries custom geo properties. The geo property values are copied. No interpolation or blending is performed. The `indices2d` port is used to specify how geo property values from the sources are mappe...

Transfer geo properties from a source geometry to a target geometry. This is useful when building a new geometry object from an existing one, and still retaining the existing geometry's custom geo properties. The geo property values are copied. No interpolation or blending is performed. The `indices` port is used to specify how geo property values from the source are mapped to the target.

Transfer geo properties using weighted sum to linearly interpolate geo properties from a source geometry to a target geometry. If a property's type is not supported (See `sample_any_array_by_weighted_sum`), the closest index property will be transfered.

Geometry::Query::build_closest_accelerat.summary: Builds an acceleration structure to be used with the `sample_closest_accelerator` and other query nodes. You can build the accelerator once, and use it in many places in a graph. However, the accelerator does not get updated automatically if the geometry is modified downstream of this node. To query the modified geometry, a build a new accelerator.

Geometry::Query::build_raycast_accelerat.summary: Builds an acceleration structure to be used with the `sample_raycast_accelerator` node. You can build the accelerator once, and use it in many places in a graph. However, the accelerator does not get updated automatically if the geometry is modified downstream of this node. To query the modified geometry, a build a new accelerator.

Geometry::Query::generate_sample_locatio.summary: Generates random locations on a geometric object.

Geometry::Query::get_closest_locations.summary: Returns the the array of locations on the input geometry's surface that are closest to each of the input positions. You can then use `sample_property` to get the interpolated values of properties on the geometry at those locations.

Geometry::Query::get_closest_point.summary: Returns the locations and indices of the points (vertices) on the input geometry that are closest to each of the input positions. You can then use `sample_property` to get the interpolated values of properties on the geometry at those locations.

Geometry::Query::get_points_in_radius.summary: Returns the locations of the points on the input geometry that are within the specified radius of  the input positions. You can then use `sample_property_2D` to get the interpolated values of properties on the geometry at those locations.

Geometry::Query::get_raycast_locations.summary: Returns the locations of the closest intersection of rays on the surface of a geometry. You can then use `sample_property` to get the interpolated values of properties on the geometry at those locations.

Geometry::Query::location_is_valid.summary: Given a location, returns whether that location is valid. An invalid location results from a search finding nothing - for example, a ray-cast missing the geometry entirely.

Geometry::Query::sample_closest_accelera.summary: Returns the closest locations on the surface of a geometry, using an acceleration structure built with a `build_closest_accelerator` node as an input.

Geometry::Query::sample_closest_in_radiu.summary: Returns the indices of the points of a geometry that are within a distance from the given positions, using an acceleration structure built with a `build_closest_accelerator` node as an input.

Geometry::Query::sample_closest_point_ac.summary: Returns the index of the points (vertices) of a geometry that are closest to each of the given positions, using an acceleration structure built with a `build_closest_accelerator` node as an input.

Geometry::Query::sample_points_by_radius.summary: Sample points by radius does a weighted average of a point `property`.

Geometry::Query::sample_property.summary: Returns the value of a property at locations on a geometry. Values can be interpolated from the closest geometric components.

Geometry::Query::sample_property_2D.summary: Returns the values of a property at locations on a geometry. Values can be interpolated from the closest geometric components.

Geometry::Query::sample_raycast_accelera.summary: Returns the location of the closest intersection of rays cast onto a geometry, using an acceleration structure built with a `build_raycast_accelerator` node as an input.

Geometry::Query::sample_volume.summary: This node samples a volume at a number of point positions.

Geometry::Query::sample_volume_gradient.summary: This node samples the gradient of a volume at a number of point positions.

Geometry::Query::sample_volume_vector.summary: This node samples a volume at a number of point positions.

Geometry::Strands::Internal::set_strands.summary: Creates strands that start at `root_positions` and extend in the directions specified by `root_normals`.

Geometry::Strands::construct_strands.summary: Constructs a `strands` geometry - creating a `strands` from raw data in the graph. This creates a minimal `strands` object, it does not set `point_size`, `point_tangent`, or any other optional properties.

Geometry::Strands::get_strands_structure.summary: Gets the canonical data for a strands geometry (point and strand counts, and the `point_position` and `strand_offset` arrays)

Geometry::Strands::resample_strands.summary: Resamples the input strands based on a spatial distance (distance between resampled points) or a constant count (total number of resampled points along the strand).  The compound supports spatial distance arrays of per-strand data (2d arrays), arrays of data (1d array), single floats and fields.  The compound will also transfer some or all of the properties from the incoming strands to the resm...

Geometry::Strands::set_strands_shape.summary: The full compound name is: Geometry::Strands::set_strands_shape

Geometry::Strands::strands_basis_to_orie.summary: Converts strand basis vectors (`point_tangent`, `point_normal`) to the `point_orientation` property. This allows each point of the strands to be used as the point cloud for instancing, placing an instance at each point with an orientation derived from a normals and tangents.

Geometry::Strands::update_point_strand_i.summary: Generates the array `point_strand_index` which specify to which individual strand each point belongs.

Geometry::Strands::update_strands_basis.summary: Generates `point_normal`, `point_tangent`, and `point_binormal` vectors for every point in the strand.  These can be used to provide an orientation along the curve.

Geometry::Strands::update_strands_length.summary: Calculates the length of strands and the segment length per point of the strands, and stores them as geo properties.

Geometry::Strands::update_strands_point_.summary: Calculates the point neighbors of each point in a strands geometry.

Geometry::Strands::update_strands_ratio.summary: Calculates the ratio at each point along the strand. The ratio is a 0-1 value, from root to tip. This node then sets or updates the `point_ratio` property. The ratio is not based on length, but is based on the strand's topology.

Geometry::Strands::update_strands_tangen.summary: Calculates tangents based on the direction to the next point in each strand, and then sets or updates the `point_tangent` property.

Geometry::Strands::validate_strands.summary: Validate that the given object adheres to the strands schema and that it contains valid data.

Geometry::Tags::Internal::convert_tag_da.summary: Converts tag data from one component type to another.

Geometry::Tags::Internal::resolve_expres.summary: Evaluates a tag expression and computes the resultant tag.

Geometry::Tags::convert_tag.summary: Convert a component tag from one component type to another. For example convert a face tag to a point tag.

Geometry::Tags::get_component_tag.summary: Gets the component tag data for a specific component tag. A tag expression can be also be used.

Geometry::Tags::interpret_auto_port_as_c.summary: Converts various inputs into type `array<bool>` and `array<long>`. This utility node lets you build reusable compounds that support multiple input types to select points or other components on a geometry to operate on. For example, you can use it to specify which points to delete in a `delete_points` compound.

Geometry::Tags::merge_tag_data.summary: Merges tag data (boolean arrays) from two different tags.

Geometry::Tags::resolve_tag_expression.summary: Resolve a tag expression. A single tag name can also be used.

Geometry::Tags::set_component_tag.summary: Creates a named component tag on a geometric object and assigns its members.

Geometry::Tags::tag_by_angle_between_vec.summary: Tag elements if the angle between different vectors is within some threshold. For example, this could be used to tag points on a mesh whose normals are pointing upward, and the resulting tag weights can be passed into `scatter_points` to scatter snow just on the upward facing parts of the mesh.

Geometry::Tags::tag_by_expression.summary: Tags geometry components whose property values match the `expression`. For example, this could be used to tag points that have values matching the `expression`.

Geometry::Tags::tag_by_threshold.summary: Tags geometry components whose property values are inside a threshold. For example this could be used to tag points that have a float property lower than a maximum, higher than a minimum, or within an interval.

Geometry::Tags::tag_inside_geometry.summary: Tag elements that are contained within another geometry. For example this could be used to tag points that are inside a bounding mesh. The output weights are the signed distances from the elements to the surface of the `bounding_geometry`. Points inside will have positive distance values, and points outside will have negative distance values. Points on the surface will have zero distance values.

Geometry::Tags::tag_randomly.summary: Tag random elements based on a probability weight threshold. A random number is generated for each element, and if the number is less than the specified `probability_weight`, it is tagged.

Geometry::Tags::tag_strand_ends.summary: Tag strands by their end points. Use the `invert_tag` port to tag points in the middle of the strands instead of the end points. Some possible uses of this node are to cut the ends off strands using `delete_points` or to place instances at the end of each strand.

Geometry::Topology::add_points.summary: Adds points to a points object, such as a particle system. Any properties that target `point_component` get set to their default value for the new points, but you can use `new_collection` to initialize them to other values.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::compute_volu.summary: This node computes the voxel_depth property from the voxel_signed_distance property on the volume.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::get_volume_t.summary: The node gets the tile info from the input volume.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::get_voxel_co.summary: The node gets the voxel count from the volume.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::get_voxel_si.summary: The node gets the voxel size from the volume.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::infinity_nor.summary: This node returns the infinity norm - i.e. the maximum length/magnitude - of the specified property in the input volume.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::merge_volume.summary: The node merges a number of input volumes.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::refine_inter.summary: This node refines the interior of a `volume` where the values of the `property` are negative.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::resample_vol.summary: This node resamples the voxel properties from `source_volume` to identically named properties on `resampled_volume`.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::scale_proper.summary: This node scales all values in the voxel property by the input scale.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::set_resoluti.summary: This node creates a "Resolution Field" structure.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::set_voxel_si.summary: The node sets the voxel size on the volume.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::sharpen_voxe.summary: This node sharpens a voxel property of name 'property'. Note that this has no effect on the visual appearance of signed distance fields.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::smooth_level.summary: This node smooths a level set surface property of name 'property' with a specified filter. The surface property is assumed to be a level set represented as a signed distance field. The level set surface is tracked by adjusting the spatial resolution as the surface moves during the filtering.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::smooth_voxel.summary: This node smooths a voxel property of name 'property' with a filter defined by the given mode, standard deviation and filter width.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::snap_to_sour.summary: This node snaps the point positions e.g. of a mesh closer to the source points from which the volume and mesh were generated.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::update_voxel.summary: This node creates a new float3 voxel channel named `voxel_position` on the volume and initializes it with the worldspace positions of the voxels using the offset provided in the voxel_offset parameter.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::validate_vol.summary: This node ensures that a valid (non-null) object is always output.

Geometry::Volume::Internal::wide_laplaci.summary: This node laplacian smooths the point_position with a weight given by the input volume (It is called wide because it smoothes based on the 2-ring of each vertex)

Geometry::Volume::analyze_volume.summary: This node analyzes a number of properties on the input volume and outputs a volume with new result properties added.

Geometry::Volume::close_holes_in_level_s.summary: This node closes holes interior to a level set as well as holes inbetween the level set and additional level set solids. For example, if the level set comes from a liquid simulation, this node can be used to close small air bubbles as well as gaps inbetween the liquid and solid colliders.

Geometry::Volume::coarsen_refine.summary: This node coarsens and/or refines a volume based on a property on the volume itself or a field.

Geometry::Volume::coarsen_voxel_property.summary: Reduces the detail of a volume based on the values of the specified property. This can be useful to reduce the memory requirement of volumes imported from VBD files.

Geometry::Volume::grade_volume.summary: This node will grade a volume such that neighboring tiles differ by at most one level.

Geometry::Volume::invert_level_set.summary: This node inverts a level such that the interior becomes the exterior and vice versa. The default value remains unchanged.

Geometry::Volume::offset_level_set.summary: This node applies a uniform offset to a level set. New tiles will be added as appropriate to keep the level set at the same resolution.

Geometry::Volume::points_to_liquid_surfa.summary: This compound is specifically designed for use with liquid simulations. Other particle based simulations or points may also work well from the included filtering and convenience that this node provides over individual, simpler nodes such as `points_to_volume`.

Geometry::Volume::rebuild_level_set.summary: This node redistances the input level set to have unit gradient. The resulting level set will be in signed distance representation.

Geometry::Volume::remap_property.summary: This node remaps all the values in the range [min, max] in voxel property of name 'property' to the new range [new_min, new_max]. The min and max are found in the property and not user-specified.

Geometry::Volume::resample_volume.summary: This node resamples the voxel properties from `source_volume` to identically named properties on `resampled_volume`.

Geometry::Volume::resize_level_set.summary: This node resizes the "narrow-band" around the level set so that it guarantees high-resolution voxels in a band of `bandwidth` voxel-space units around the level set. Note that if there are already more tiles than necessary to guarantee a bandwidth of `bandwidth`, extraneous tiles will be removed.

Geometry::Volume::sharpen_voxel_property.summary: This node sharpens a voxel property of name 'property'.

Geometry::Volume::smooth_level_set_prope.summary: This node smooths a level set surface property of name `property` with a specified filter. The surface property is assumed to be a level set represented as a signed distance field. The level set surface is tracked by adjusting the spatial resolution as the surface moves during the filtering.

Geometry::Volume::smooth_voxel_property.summary: This node smooths a voxel property of name `property` with a filter defined by the given mode, standard deviation and filter width.

Geometry::Volume::smooth_voxel_temperatu.summary: The node remaps the temperature property with a smooth falloff near the edges of the visible voxel_fog_density. This creates a smoother black body radiation rendering.

Geometry::Volume::splat_points_into_volu.summary: This node splats points into the properties of the input/output volume. If the points come with a radius channel, the associated radius will be used when splatting the points. Otherwise, the value on the input radius port will be used. Note, currently when splatting to coarser levels, the input radius port is used even when the points have a radius channel.

Geometry::Volume::update_voxel_position.summary: This node creates a new float3 voxel channel named `voxel_position` on the volume and initializes it with the worldspace positions of the voxels using the offset provided in the voxel_offset parameter.

Geometry::Volume::volume_bounds.summary: This node computes the minimum and maximum bounds of a volume. Any level set or fog density volume is taken into account and in case both exists, the union of the two bounds is returned.

MachineLearning::Activation::activation_.summary: Continuously Differentiable Exponential Linear Unit (CELU) activation function helps to mitigate the vanishing gradient problem for negative input values and has mean activations near zero.
The Exponential Linear Unit (ELU) activation function helps to mitigate the vanishing gradient problem for negative input values.
The Parametric Rectified Linear Unit (PReLU) activation function that generalizes the traditional rectified unit with a slope for negative values.
The Randomized Leaky Rectified Linear Unit (RReLU) activation function that randomly samples the negative slope for activations from a uniform distribution.
The Rectified Linear Unit (ReLU) activation function which transforms negative input values to 0 and retains positive input values.

The Rectified Linear Unit - 6 (ReLU6) activation function is a modification if the ReLU activation function where the activation is limited to a value of 6. This provides increased robustness when used with low-precision computation
The Scaled Exponential Linear Unit (SELU) activation function, which induce self-normalizing properties.

The Hard Shrink activation function sets the output to zero for inputs within a certain range around zero (typically between -0.5 and 0.5), and retains the input values outside of that range unchanged.

The Hard Sigmoid activation function approximates the Sigmoid function by using a simple piecewise linear function that clamps the output between 0 and 1 for inputs outside a specified range, while linearly scaling inputs within that range.
The Hard Swish activation function multiplies the input by a clipped version of itself, blending the input with a hard sigmoid function to control the output's range and non-linearity.
The Hard Tanh activation function clamps the output to be within the range of `min_val` and `max_val`, acting like a tanh function but with a piecewise linear approximation.
The Leaky ReLU activation function allows a small, non-zero gradient when the input is less than zero, which helps maintain the flow of gradients during training.
The Log Sigmoid activation function outputs the logarithm of the sigmoid function, providing a transformation that is useful in cases where the logarithm of probability is needed.
The Mish activation function applies a smooth, self-regularized non-linear activation that multiplies the input by the softplus of the input, supporting deeper network training without saturation.
The Sigmoid activation function maps the input values into a range between 0 and 1, providing a smooth transition similar to a step function.
The softmax activation function is used to normalize an input vector into a probability distribution over multiple classes, such that the elements of the output vector sum to 1.
The Softmin activation function applies the softmax function to the negatives of the input values, resulting in a distribution where the smallest input gets the highest probability.
The Softplus activation function provides a smooth approximation of the ReLU function, gradually transitioning outputs from zero to positive values based on the input.
The Soft Shrink activation function applies a soft version of thresholding that shifts inputs towards zero by a threshold value, but does not set small inputs exactly to zero.
The Softsign activation function divides the input by the sum of its absolute value and 1, producing an output that is bounded between -1 and 1 but with gentler saturation than tanh.
The Tanh activation function maps the input to values between -1 and 1, providing a scaled and shifted output that helps in normalizing the data flow in the network.
The Tanh Shrink activation function computes the difference between the input and its tanh, effectively reducing the magnitude of the input while maintaining signs.
The Threshold activation function sets the output to a fixed value if the input is below a certain threshold, and retains the input value otherwise, acting as a form of step function.

MachineLearning::Layer::layer_linear.summary: Performs the linear transformation for a layer in a neural network - the foundation of the feedforward mechanism in neural networks. After this linear operation, an activation function (like ReLU, sigmoid, etc.) is typically applied to introduce non-linearity.

MachineLearning::Utils::z_score_denormal.summary: Removes normalization on input vector based on feature-wise mean and standard deviation.

MachineLearning::Utils::z_score_normaliz.summary: Normalizes input vector using feature-wise mean and standard deviation.

Modeling::Common::delete_points.summary: Returns a new point-based geometry (such as a particle system or mesh) without the specified points.

Modeling::Common::merge_geometry.summary: Merges an array of geometric objects into a single one. The objects should all be the same type, for example, all meshes, or all points objects, and so on. If the array contains different types of geometry, only those objects with the same type as the first object in the array get merged.

Modeling::Converters::Internal::convert_.summary: Voxelizes the input geometry to create a level-set (signed-distance field) and/or a fog-density volume. This node can also voxelize other properties stored on the input geometry.

Modeling::Converters::convert_to_volume.summary: Voxelizes the input geometry to create a level-set (signed-distance field) and/or a fog-density volume. This node can also voxelize other properties stored on the input geometry.

Modeling::Instances::bake_instanced_geom.summary: Converts instances into non-instanced geometry. It builds a combined mesh, combined strands, or combined point clouds from all the geometry that was instanced on the inputs.

Modeling::Instances::create_instances.summary: Creates an instance object consisting of shapes attached to the point positions of the input geometry. Multiple shapes are supported, and can be assigned in various ways.

Modeling::Internal::filter_indexed_array.summary: This is useful when modifying an indexed geo property like UVs. It can be used to retain the UVs only for a specific set of face vertices.

Modeling::Knits::create_stitch.summary: Create a stitch mesh from a stitch template and a polygon.

Modeling::Knits::create_stitch_template.summary: Create a stitch template from a polygon and strands.

Modeling::Knits::create_strands_from_sti.summary: Create strands from a stitch mesh.

Modeling::Mesh::Internal::filter_UVs.summary: Discard UV data elements that are only referenced by faces that will be re-mapped and then compact the UV data array.

Modeling::Mesh::boolean_fracture_mesh.summary: This node slices an input mesh using an array of meshes. One may optionally generate planes to act as slicer meshes which combine with any input slicer meshes. Shards are only created where a mesh slices all the way through a mesh. A partial intersection will have no effect.

Modeling::Mesh::boolean_meshes.summary: Perform a boolean operation on the input meshes. This node can be used to carve out one mesh from another, combine multiple meshes to form a single mesh, or to determine where the input meshes overlap in space.

Modeling::Mesh::cluster_voronoi_shards.summary: This compound combines shards created by the `voronoi_fracture_mesh` compound into larger clusters, which can help create fracture pieces that have a less regular look. The shards are combined based on cellular noise sampled at the center of the bounding box of each shard.

Modeling::Mesh::compute_convex_hull.summary: This node computes the convex hull of the point positions of the input geometry.

Modeling::Mesh::compute_voronoi_diagram.summary: This node computes the 3d voronoi diagram from a set of points and outputs a cell corresponding to each point. Every point within the volume of a cell is closest to that cell's corresponding input point.

Modeling::Mesh::create_UVs_from_projecti.summary: Create a UV mapping for the specified faces of the input mesh by projecting those faces onto planes arranged spherically around the mesh.

Modeling::Mesh::create_slicer_planes.summary: This node generate a grid of planes for use by `fracture_mesh`. The planes will be fit to the bounds of the input object.

Modeling::Mesh::delete_faces.summary: Returns a new mesh object without the specified faces. Vertices that aren't referenced by any of the kept faces are also discarded.

Modeling::Mesh::delete_isolated_points.summary: "Cleans" a mesh by removing points that are not used by any face.

Modeling::Mesh::delete_mesh_points.summary: Removes points from a mesh, removing also any faces they are connected to.

Modeling::Mesh::detach_faces.summary: Disconnects the specified `faces` from the rest of the mesh. The points on the border between these faces and other faces in the mesh are duplicated and the `faces` are modified to reference the new points. If `duplicate_all_border_points` is checked, all the border is duplicated, and some points may be left isolated.

Modeling::Mesh::disconnect_mesh_faces.summary: Creates a mesh where faces no longer share vertices and each face is disconnected. This means the new mesh will have a point for each face-vertex of the old mesh.

Modeling::Mesh::extrude_faces.summary: Extrudes the specified faces of an input mesh. This detaches the specified faces, offsets them by the `thickness` input, and inserts new faces between the specified faces and the faces they were adjacent to. The specified faces will be kept together in the output mesh.

Modeling::Mesh::filter_faces.summary: Creates a new mesh containing only the specified faces from the input mesh.

Modeling::Mesh::find_isolated_points.summary: Returns the indices of points in a mesh that are not referenced by any face.

Modeling::Mesh::fracture_mesh.summary: This node fractures a mesh into multiple shards.

Modeling::Mesh::layout_UVs.summary: Pack UVs of meshes in a given tile space. They are packed in the [0,1] tile space by default. The UVs of each mesh are packed with respect to the UVs of the other meshes so that they do not overlap with each other.

Modeling::Mesh::reverse_face_orientation.summary: Reverse the winding order of the specified input faces by reversing their face vertices. This is useful for fixing meshes that contain faces with inconsistent winding orders. See `find_face_orientations` for more details.

Modeling::Mesh::separate_mesh.summary: Separates a single mesh with multiple islands into multiple, individual meshes. Conceptually, this is the opposite of `merge_geometry`. Each island is a group of faces that are connected to each other. A face can belong to only one island.

Modeling::Mesh::subdivide_mesh.summary: Subdivides a mesh using various subdivision schemes. This node refines the mesh geometry by adding new vertices and faces according to the specified subdivision algorithm.

Modeling::Mesh::unify_face_orientations.summary: Ensure all of the faces in the input mesh have a consistent winding order. This node will flip individual faces of the mesh to ensure that all faces conform to the same winding order. By default, this node will select the smallest group of faces to flip. The `invert` flag will invert this logic.

Modeling::Mesh::voronoi_fracture_mesh.summary: This node creates Voronoi cells from input points and fractures an input mesh with these cells. The points for the cell centers may be both procedurally generated and directly input.

Modeling::Points::cull_overlapping_point.summary: The `merged_points` output will contain all the `static_points` as well as additional points from `candidate_points` that are not within `radius` from any other points in the output.

Modeling::Points::cull_points.summary: Randomly deletes points on a points object such as a particle system, based on weighted probabilities. In the case of an instances object, you can disable points instead — that is, prevent an instanced geometry from appearing at a point without deleting the point.

Modeling::Points::delete_points_in_point.summary: Removes points from a points object, such as a particle system.

Modeling::Points::displace_points.summary: Displaces a geometry's points along the given vectors.

Modeling::Points::duplicate_points.summary: Duplicates the specified points. All specified per-point properties will also be duplicated. This is valid for all point-based geometry types (points, strands, and meshes).

Modeling::Points::orient_points_by_geome.summary: Sets the `point_orientation` property of a point-based object based on sampling a mesh geometry. The Y axis of the orientation is aligned with the geometry's normal, and the other axes are aligned with its tangent plane. For example, this is useful for aligning instances that have been scattered on a landscape mesh.

Modeling::Points::randomize_point_rotati.summary: Randomizes the `point_orientation` property. This affects the orientation of instances, as well as point shapes (if they are not aligned to the camera). However, it does not affect the rotation of the geometric object as a whole.

Modeling::Points::randomize_point_scale.summary: Randomizes the `point_scale` property. This affects the size of instances, as well as point shapes. However, it does not affect the size of the geometric object as a whole.

Modeling::Points::randomize_selection.summary: Randomizes the shapes placed on the points of an instances object.

Modeling::Points::randomize_selection_by.summary: Randomizes the shapes placed on the points of an instances object, with control over the relative numbers of each shape.

Modeling::Points::rotate_points.summary: Updates the current `point_orientation` values of a point-based geometry by the specified rotation. This affects the orientation of instances, as well as point shapes (if they are not aligned to the camera). However, it does not affect the rotation of the geometric object as a whole.
