Modeling::Points::scale_points.summary: Multiplies the current `point_scale` values of a point-based geometry by the specified scaling factor. This affects the size of instances, as well as point shapes. However, it does not affect the size of the geometric object as a whole.

Modeling::Points::scatter_points.summary: Generates a points object whose points are distributed across a geometry. For example, this is useful for instancing things like plants and rocks on a landscape. In addition, this compound outputs the corresponding point positions as well as the geo locations in case you want to sample other properties on the geometry.

Modeling::Points::scatter_points_blue_no.summary: Scatters points on the input geometry, following a "blue noise" pattern — points won't be too close to each other, and there won't be large gaps between the points. This is also referred to as a "quasi-random" or "low discrepancy" distribution.

Modeling::Points::transform_points.summary: Transforms a point-based geometry by a 4x4 matrix. The effect is the similar to parenting the geometry to the transformation, and baking the results into world space. In the case of points and instances, the effect can be applied in local space.

Modeling::Points::translate_points.summary: Offsets the `point_position` property of a point-based geometry by the specified translation.

Modeling::Primitive::create_mesh_capsule.summary: Create a capsule mesh with normals and UVs.  A capsule is a cylinder with spherical caps.

Modeling::Primitive::create_mesh_cube.summary: Creates a mesh cube with normals.

Modeling::Primitive::create_mesh_cylinde.summary: Create a cylinder mesh with normals and UVs.

Modeling::Primitive::create_mesh_plane.summary: Creates a mesh plane with normals.

Modeling::Primitive::create_mesh_sphere.summary: Creates a mesh sphere with normals.

Modeling::Primitive::create_mesh_torus.summary: Creates a mesh torus with normals and UVs.

Modeling::Strands::create_arrow_strands.summary: Creates arrows out from strands for diagnostic purposes. Arrow strands are four vertex strands where thickness (point_size) is used to create an arrow shape. They are displayed as ribbons.

Modeling::Strands::create_strands_around.summary: This compound uses `strands_basis` and `point_ratio` to create new strands around input strands. Modeling::Strands::delete_strands.summary: Removes the specified strands from a strands object.

Modeling::Strands::delete_strands_points.summary: Removes the specified points indices from a strands object.

Modeling::Strands::filter_strands.summary: Creates a new strands object containing only the specified strands from the input.

Modeling::Strands::points_array_to_stran.summary: Creates strand trails from an array of point-based geometries. Trails will connect the first point of each geometry to each other.

Modeling::Strands::separate_strands.summary: Separates a strand into multiple, individual strands.

Modeling::Strands::smooth_strands.summary: Smoothes the values of geo properties on a strands object by averaging each point's value with those of its neighbors along the same strand.

Modeling::Volume::merge_volumes.summary: The combine volume compound serves the purpose of merging volumes while providing options for how the information is combined for level sets, fog density, and other data present in the objects.

Modeling::Volume::remap_fog_density.summary: This compound allows you to directly edit your fog density in a `fog_density` based volume or aero output. The compound contains controls that will allow you to fine-tune, erode and edit your fog volumes.

Rendering::Arnold::Arnold_Alembic_instan.summary: Creates an instance shape that references an Alembic file on disk. The instance shape can be connected into `create_instances`, `set_instance_shape`, `set_instance_geometry`, or `selector_instance`. This creates an Alembic procedural node when rendering with Arnold.

Rendering::Arnold::Arnold_ray_bitmask.summary: To be used in conjunction with the set_Arnold_* nodes, which set Arnold-specific geometry settings. In Arnold several visibility settings are set per-ray type, including `autobump`, `sidedness`, and `visibility`. These are encoded as bitmasks. This node allows constructing such a mask. Rendering::Arnold::Arnold_standard_volum.summary: Creates a material definition with the same property names as an Arnold standard volume material.

Rendering::Arnold::set_Arnold_geo_settin.summary: Sets Arnold-specific settings on a `geometry`, to be applied in Arnold as Arnold-native settings. These settings are shared by all Arnold geometry types. These settings do not affect the viewport, only Arnold rendering.

Rendering::Arnold::set_Arnold_mesh_setti.summary: Sets Arnold-specific `mesh` (in Arnold: `polygons`) settings, to be applied in Arnold as Arnold-native settings. These settings do not affect the viewport, only Arnold rendering.

Rendering::Arnold::set_Arnold_points_set.summary: Sets Arnold-specific `points` (in Arnold: `particles`) settings, to be applied in Arnold as Arnold-native settings. These settings do not affect the viewport, only Arnold rendering.

Rendering::Arnold::set_Arnold_strands_se.summary: Sets Arnold-specific `strands` (in Arnold: `curves`) settings, to be applied in Arnold as Arnold-native settings. These settings do not affect the viewport, only Arnold rendering.

Rendering::Arnold::set_Arnold_volume_set.summary: Sets Arnold-specific `volume` settings, to be applied in Arnold as Arnold-native settings. These settings do not effect the viewport, only Arnold rendering.

Rendering::Materials::assign_material.summary: Assigns a material to a geometric object.

Rendering::Materials::constant_surface_m.summary: Creates a simple material with a constant color.

Rendering::Materials::set_geo_property_r.summary: Drives a material parameter by a geo property on an object.

Rendering::Materials::standard_surface_m.summary: Creates a material definition with the same property names as the standard surface material.

Rendering::Motion_Blur::set_motion_blur_.summary: Stores a property on a geometric object that can be used by a compatible renderer to control how motion blur is rendered.

Rendering::Terminals::final_mode.summary: Final mode node to indicate if the "final" terminal port is being evaluated or not.

Rigging::Module::Animation::find_upstrea.summary: Finds an upstream transform of a control or a joint in parent modules whose name matches a specified search pattern expression, or whose tags match a list of tags to find.

Rigging::Module::template_module.summary: A template rigging module to be used to create your own. Users are expected to make this compound editable and implement their module's setup compute and animation solve in the dedicated `user_setup` and `user_animation` sub-compounds.

Rigging::Skeleton::construct_skeleton.summary: Constructs a skeleton geometry with only the properties that are required for a valid skeleton structure.

Rigging::Skeleton::get_joint_transform_m.summary: Get all eight geo property `array<double4x4>` data containing the joints' transform matrix values.

Rigging::Skeleton::get_skeleton_structur.summary: Gets the canonical data for a skeleton geometry.

Rigging::Skeleton::set_joint_operator_ma.summary: Sets the `joint_operator_matrix` geo property data into a skeleton.

Rigging::Skeleton::set_joint_pivot_matri.summary: Sets the `joint_pivot_matrix` geo property data into a skeleton.

Rigging::Skeleton::transform_joints.summary: Transforms all or any joints, and propagate the transformation changes to all of their respective descendants.

Rigging::Skeleton::update_chain_joint_in.summary: Updates the ordered list of joint indices contained within each chains of the skeleton.

Rigging::Skeleton::update_joint_chain_in.summary: Updates the joint chain indices, meaning the index of the chain a joint belongs to.

Rigging::Skeleton::update_joint_children.summary: Updates the joint children indices of each joints.

Rigging::Skeleton::update_joint_depth.summary: Updates the joint depths, meaning how deep a joint is in the hierarchy, relative to their respective roots.

Rigging::Skeleton::update_joint_length.summary: Updates the joint absolute lengths, meaning their total distance to their relative roots, by walking the joint hierarchy tree.

Rigging::Skeleton::update_joint_path.summary: Updates the joint paths with default joint names.

Rigging::Skeleton::update_joint_position.summary: Updates the joint positions from their transform matrices.

Rigging::Skeleton::update_joint_transfor.summary: Updates all eight `array<double4x4>` joint transform geo properties of a skeleton based on the `joint_pivot_matrix` and `joint_operator_matrix` geo properties in order to update the full joint transform data.

Rigging::Skeleton::validate_skeleton.summary: Validates a skeleton by checking if it complies with the requirements of the skeleton schema.

Rigging::Solver::Utils::calculate_pole_t.summary: Calculates the position of a pole target based on three input vectors or three transformation matrices.

Rigging::Solver::Utils::enabled_with_wei.summary: Checks if both a `bool` toggle is active, and a scalar weight is greater than zero.

Rigging::Solver::Utils::equivalent_weigh.summary: Checks if a weight value is almost equal to zero or one.

Rigging::Solver::aim_matrix.summary: Orients a transform matrix so that its specified primary and secondary axes points toward specified primary and secondary targets.

Rigging::Solver::align_matrix_chain.summary: Transforms a selected range of a transform matrices to align them toward a specified target vector.

Rigging::Solver::blend_matrix.summary: Blends a transform matrix with specified targets.

Rigging::Solver::interpolate_matrix_chai.summary: Blends between two continuous chains of transform matrices using local space interpolation.

Rigging::Solver::offset_matrix_chain.summary: Translates a selected range of a transform matrices by offsetting their positions.

Rigging::Solver::orient_matrix_chain.summary: Orients a selected range of transform matrices to make them aim toward their successors in the chain.

Rigging::Solver::parent_matrix.summary: Blends a transform matrix with specified targets in a parenting-like manner.

Rigging::Solver::pick_matrix.summary: Creates a new transform matrix containing the selected transform components from an input transform.

Rigging::Solver::resample_matrix_chain.summary: Resamples a transform matrix chain using various resampling methods and options.

Rigging::Solver::scale_matrix_chain.summary: Translates a selected range of a transform matrices as if scaling was applied to them from a specified parent point.

Rigging::Solver::simulate_rods.summary: Simulates transform matrices as Cosserat rods. Both chain and tree topologies are supported. The topology is defined by the `parent_indices`, allowing for continuous or branched rod structures. When the `parent_indices` port is unconnected, the input `transforms` are treated as a continuous chain. When connected, arbitrary hierarchical relationships can be defined.

Rigging::Solver::solve_limb_IK.summary: Performs two bone inverse kinematic on a transform matrix chain.

Rigging::Solver::transform_matrix_chain.summary: Transforms a selected range of a transform matrices by another transform.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::add_buoyancy.summary: This node adds buoyant acceleration to the velocity field of the input body and places the result in outBody.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::add_buoyant_.summary: This node computes buoyant acceleration of the input body and adds it to the in/out array.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::aero_body.summary: This node creates an empty aero body with a voxeltopology, a container as well as smoke density and temperature channels.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::aero_point_b.summary: This node creates an empty aero body with a container as well as point velocity, smoke density and temperature channels.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::create_impro.summary: This node adds the channels required for improved time integration to the input object.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::emit.summary: This node emits into an aero body and places the result in outAeroBody.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::emit_points.summary: This node emits points into the bif Object.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::min_fluid_de.summary: This node finds the mininum fluid_detail_size of the input sources

Simulation::Aero::Internal::min_start_fr.summary: This node finds the mininum startFrame property of the input sources

Simulation::Aero::Internal::set_refineme.summary: This node sets the depth of the upres channels defined by aero_solver_settings

Simulation::Aero::Internal::split_points.summary: The node "splits" points to alleviate the grainy look that can sometimes result from splatting points with a poor spatial distribution. The observation is that we can avoid a grainy look by ensuring a smooth distribution of density on the points. Thus, we sample new points whenever we detect points that too far away from the average of the points in a given voxel.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::to_aero_tran.summary: This node converts a value of type TransportStyle to TransportInterpolationType.

Simulation::Aero::Internal::to_areo_tran.summary: This node converts a value of type TransportInterpolationType to TransportStyle.

Simulation::Aero::aero_adaptivity_settin.summary: Defines regions of different detail (spatially adaptive resolution) for aero and combustion simulations. This connects to the `additional_settings` port of the `aero_solver_settings` node.

Simulation::Aero::aero_color_post_proces.summary: This node can be used post aero simulation to keep emitted colors from going dark over time. If one uses aero_source_color property to create a color property then a voxel_emission_density property is created than can be used by this node to unpremultiply the colors. As well there is a step that dilates colors outward to avoid dark fringes in the final render.

Simulation::Aero::aero_combustion_settin.summary: Sets options for combustion simulations. Connect the output of this node to the `additional_settings` port of an `aero_solver_settings` node.

Simulation::Aero::aero_refinement_settin.summary: Sets options for aero simulation refinement and sharpening. The output of this node should be connected to the `additional_settings` input of an `aero_solver_settings` node.

Simulation::Aero::aero_solver_settings.summary: Sets options for aero and combustion simulations. The output of this node should be connected to the `settings` input of a `simulate_aero` node.

Simulation::Aero::aero_uvw_settings.summary: Creates a number of UVW coordinate sets that gets advected with an aero simulation. This compound plugs into the `addtional_settings` port on the `aero_solver_settings` compound. The resulting property represents UVW coordinates for the entire aero body.

Simulation::Aero::basic_aero_graph.summary: The `basic_aero_graph` sets up a simple graph that produces a rising smoke plume. Add this node at the top level of a graph, explode it, and connect its inputs and outputs.

Simulation::Aero::basic_combustion_graph.summary: The `basic_combustion_graph` sets up a simple graph that produces an explosion followed by a rising smoke plume. Add this node at the top level of a graph, explode it, and connect its inputs and outputs.

Simulation::Aero::condense_water_vapor.summary: The node condenses the water vapor property based on the temperature property and a computation of the relative humidity inside the user-specified temperature interval, which in reality is 0 to 100 degrees Celcius. The water vapor property on the output object will only be non-zero where the water vapor property on the input object has condensed. For artistic effects, a pair of min and max temp...

Simulation::Aero::post_refine_aero.summary: Adds high-resolution detail to enhance the look of aero and combustion simulations. The resolution of all properties except velocity is increased. This can give good-looking results for a simulation with low resolution (high detail size), while still being faster than a high-resolution simulation.

Simulation::Aero::simulate_aero.summary: The `simulate_aero` compound contains the core solver for aero and combustion simulations.

Simulation::Aero::source_air.summary: Specifies the parameters of a source that emits properties into the simulation grid.

Simulation::Aero::source_fuel.summary: Specifies the parameters of a fuel source that emits properties into the simulation grid. This should be connected to the `additional_properties` input on a `source_air` node. Several `source_fuel` nodes can be connected to the additional_properties fan  port to form more advanced mixtures of fuel and oxidizer. For example, a MAPP gas typically used for practical VFX consists of propyne, propad...

Simulation::Aero::voxel_color_scope.summary: This allows one to easily display aero color properties by sampling points in the aero volume. The colors are shown without shading applied and may be sparcely sampled from the volume for fast updates.

Simulation::Combustion::Internal::combus.summary: This node computes the combustion specified by the input parameters and object.

Simulation::Combustion::Internal::comput.summary: This node computes the mass density from all available species and the temperature using the ideal gas law, and places the output in the voxel_mass_density property.
This node computes the fuel, nitrogen and oxygen mass fractions from the burn rate and oxygen fraction

Simulation::Combustion::Internal::create.summary: This node adds the channels required for combustion to the input object.

Simulation::Combustion::Internal::oxidiz.summary: This node computes soot oxidation in a combustion simulation. The total soot oxidation rate is a combination of a constant oxidation speed and a physics-based soot oxidation rate that depends on temperature as well as the local concentration of oxygen, fuel and soot.
This node oxidizes a level set representing the iso-contour of soot. A physics-based soot oxidation model is applied which takes into account oxygen, fuel, soot and temperature if available.
This node oxidizes soot based on the change between two level set surfaces representing an iso-contour of the soot before and after oxidation.

Simulation::Combustion::Internal::post_o.summary: This node computes soot oxidation of a combustion simulation cache as a post-process. The total soot oxidation rate is a combination of a constant oxidation speed and a physics-based soot oxidation rate that depends on temperature as well as the local concentration of oxygen, fuel and soot.

Simulation::Common::aero_source_color_pr.summary: This allows one to easily add a color property to the additional properties of an aero source_air. It additionally generates a voxel_emission_density, which can be used by aero_color_post_process post simulation to correct for darkening of colors during simulation.

Simulation::Common::collider.summary: Colliders are obstacles to the flow of a Bifrost simulation. You can use them to form a barrier around which smoke must flow, or create a basin that prevents particles from falling away under gravity. Colliders can be animated to create various effects.

Simulation::Common::compute_on_frame.summary: An experimental node which will compute a value on a certain frame, but not otherwise.

Simulation::Common::compute_point_veloci.summary: Computes the velocities between two frames for a given point geometry, and stores it on the geometry.

Simulation::Common::compute_velocity.summary: This computes the velocities between two frames for a given geometry, and stores it on the geometry. This is useful to provide velocities for moving meshes that are used in a simulation. Normally simulations will automatically compute velocities on input source or collider meshes, but this could be used for a custom solver. Another use is before a `convert_to_volume` so that the volume has velo...

Simulation::Common::create_smooth_trail.summary: This node creates a trail from an animated mesh into the input volume. The volume can be a level set (signed-distance field) and/or a fog-density volume.

Simulation::Common::file_cache.summary: An experimental node which can cache and read back simulations by writing them to a file.

Simulation::Common::force_pull_port.summary: This compound forces the graph to "pull" on a data stream and evaluate it.  It comprises a pass-through element and the stream you wish to force the graph to evaluate.

Simulation::Common::generate_pulse.summary: Generate pulse is a utility to create pulsing animations on particle properties (but could be used elsewhere) instead of having pulse attributes on the source.

Simulation::Common::memory_cache.summary: Caches an animated object or array of object to memory for faster playback once the cache is filled. This is intended to be used in the graph after a simulation, file read, or any other heavy operation to speed up its playback.  The cache can be cleared by using "Reset Feedback State" in the Bifrost "Edit" menu.

Simulation::Common::set_initial_state.summary: This compound makes the simuation read an existing file from disk and resume the simulation from that point.

Simulation::Common::should_simulate.summary: Returns the input `object` or `prev_object`, depending on whether the current time is a valid simulation step. See the `simulation_example` for a basic example of how to use this node.

Simulation::Common::simulation_example.summary: A basic example of how to setup a dynamic simulation where one uses a feedback port to maintain the dynamic state between frames, as well as `should_simulate` to determine when to solve and when to initialize. Simulation::Common::source_color_propert.summary: This allows one to easily add a color property to the additional properties of a simulation source, such as a source_particles or source_air node.

Simulation::Common::vary_source_property.summary: This compound is useful to set per-point values on simulation sources. For example you could use this compound to vary the size of the points generated in a particle simulation.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::add_accele.summary: Scales the acceleration by beta and adds it to the velocity field.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::add_vortic.summary: This node adds vorticity confinement to the velocity field of the input body and places the result in outBody.
This node adds the vorticity confinement acceleration to the acceleration array.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::build_halo.summary: Builds halo properties on the volume to avoid having to re-build these during sampling.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::coarsen_re.summary: This node coarsens and refines the container of the input body to capture all interesting features and places the result in outBody.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::compute_ad.summary: The node computes an adaptivity channel that guides the coarsen/refine node in where to refine and coarsen.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::compute_ti.summary: This node computes the time step of a sub step loop.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::debug.summary: This node allows the user to set various debug parameters that are used by the solvers to output debug information.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::debug_prin.summary: This node allows the user to insert checkpoints into the graph for debugging.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::remove_hal.summary: Removes halo properties on the volume.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::resample.summary: This node resamples the time-dependent properties of a number of voxel volumes in time to create a combined resampled volume.

Internal nodes are not intended to be used directly in graphs, but instead are used to implement more user-friendly compounds. You can make internal nodes available by setting the environment variable `BIFROST_DISABLE` to `hide-internal-nodes` before launching Bifrost's host application, but be awa...

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::solve_pres.summary: This node performs a pressure projection of the velocity field in the input body and places it in outBody.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::stash_acce.summary: The node computes and stores the acceleration based on the difference in velocity.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::stash_post.summary: The node sets the post refine velocity field (velocity_up_res) equal to the velocity.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::stash_velo.summary: The node sets the intermediate velocity field (velocity0) equal to the velocity.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::swap_upres.summary: This node swaps the upres and the non-upres channels to facilitate using standard names in the existing solvers.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::transport.summary: This node transports the channels of the input body in the velocity field of the body's voxel topology.

Simulation::Fluids::Internal::voxel_swep.summary: The node sweeps a number of voxel volumes in time to create a combined swept voxel field.

Simulation::Influence::Internal::vector_.summary: A vector field whose value at any position is the input vector.

Simulation::Influence::aero_einstein_inf.summary: This compound generates coarse and fine velocity fields and adds them to the existing aero velocity so to retain the overall shape and behavior, but with disturbance from the turbulence. Finally, vorticity is generated and added relative to the velocity.  This is an aero influence only and currently does not have any effect on particles.  To use this node, plug `turbulence_influence` and/or `vo...

Simulation::Influence::aero_erode_densit.summary: This influence erodes the density in a range of density values to, for example, counter diffusion.

Simulation::Influence::aero_noise_transp.summary: This influence randomly displaces (or transports) density using a noise. The direction of displacement is the gradient of either the density or the temperature. This can provide detail without affecting the velocity, though over time can result in some density diffusion.

Simulation::Influence::aero_pyroclastic_.summary: The `aero_pyroclastic_influence` adds detail to aero simulations that resembles the pyroclastic detail seen in volcanic plumes and large explosions.  Two separate influences, drag and vorticity, are being output and can each be inspected by the `influence_scope` with an aero object as `probe_geometry`.  To get the full pyroclastic effect, both output influences must be connected to the `simulat...

Simulation::Influence::attract_repulse_i.summary: The attract_repulse influence applies a force towards or away from an input geometry.

Simulation::Influence::boundary_drag_inf.summary: This drag_influence can be used to simulate effects of air drag along the outer boundary of clumps of particles. Simulation::Influence::buoyancy_influenc.summary: The buoyancy influence applies an acceleration proportionate to temperature along the buoyancy direction. It only works with the simulate_aero node currently, and is not support for simulate_particles.

Simulation::Influence::clamp_influence.summary: The clamp influence can be used to clamp the value of a simulation property like `voxel_density`,`point_velocity`, or `point_size`.

Simulation::Influence::collide_field_inf.summary: Allows a simulation such as particles, mpm, or aero to collide with a signed distance field (SDF), such as the output of `plane_field` or `sphere_field`. Connect a distance field and plug `out_influence` into the `influences` input of a simulate node like `simulate_aero`, `simulate_particles`, or `simulate_mpm`.

Simulation::Influence::dilate_influence.summary: The dilate influence can be used to keep emitted colors in an aero simulation from going dark over time. It propagates a defined property inside dense regions outward into zero density regions. For example if one adds voxel_color to the source then the voxels outside the emission regions will initially be black. Over time as these regions mix with the dense regions the color can turn black. Thi...

Simulation::Influence::dissipation_influ.summary: The dissipation influence will move a defined property toward a background value at a specified decay rate.

Simulation::Influence::drag_influence.summary: This drag_influence can be used to simulate effects of air drag. By its self drag_influence damps the simulation velocity. If there are any other influence nodes connected to this that add an acceleration then this will damp motion towards that accelleration, rather than zero velocity. This can simulate high drag in situations where the medium, like water, is flowing.

Simulation::Influence::foam_advect_influ.summary: This influence is designed to advect or propagate foam particles based on an input liquid volume. To use this node, plug its output into the `influences` input of a `simulate_particles` node

Simulation::Influence::fractal_disturban.summary: The disturbance influence applies a fractal disturbance noise acceleration, which is useful for effects like air turbulence.

Simulation::Influence::gravity_influence.summary: The gravity influence applies a simple acceleration along a direction.

Simulation::Influence::ground_plane_infl.summary: Allows particles, mpm, and aero simulations to collide with an implicit infinite plane, which uses less memory than explicit geometry. Plug `out_influence` into the `influences` input of a simulate node like `simulate_aero`, `simulate_particles`, or `simulate_mpm`.

Simulation::Influence::guiding_influence.summary: The `guiding_influence` sets the `voxel_velocity` of a voxel-based simulation to a combination of a `guiding_velocity` and the user-defined higher frequencies of the simulation. This allows the user to guide the simulation with a custom velocity field, while still allowing the simulation to develop its own higher frequency motion.

Simulation::Influence::influence_set_ori.summary: This allows one to set the point_orientation property on the simulation, which defines the point rotation, using a float3 or VectorField.  The point_orientation is internally maintained as a quaternion, but this node only allows setting it with euler angles or a rotation vector which then internally get converted to a quaternion. One may set point_orientation using a float4 quaternion using the...

Simulation::Influence::influence_set_pro.summary: This allows one to set a geo property on the simulation. The type of the value should match the type for the geo property, so one could use float or a scalarField for a property like `point_size`, while if setting `point_velocity` then the value should be either a float3 or vectorfield. If there is no mask for the influence it will set all values, otherwise it will respect any defined mask.

Simulation::Influence::influence_set_spi.summary: This allows one to set the `point_spin` property on the simulation, which controls the rotational velocity.  The spin is internally maintained as a rotation vector, but one may optionally set it using euler angles. One can use a vector field to set this, for more control. The current point_spin can be accessed using a proxy field, which would return a rotation vector value. Note that rotation v...

Simulation::Influence::kill_influence.summary: The kill influence removes particles or density at a defined rate. One can combine this with a mask_influence to only kill in certain regions, as well as with a modulate_influence to kill based on simulation properties.

Simulation::Influence::kill_plane_influe.summary: The kill plane influence removes all particles or fluid on the negative side of the plane.

Simulation::Influence::mask_influence.summary: The mask influence can be used to modify the amount of effect of other influence nodes using the distance to geometry. It will only have effect when combined with other influence nodes through the `influence` port. It should also have some geometry connected to the `geometry` port.

Simulation::Influence::modifier_influenc.summary: The modifier influence can be used to replace, add, multiply or clamp the value of a simulation property like `voxel_density`,`point_velocity`, or `point_size`.

Simulation::Influence::modulate_influenc.summary: The modulate influence allows one to use a simulation property to scale the amount of effect applied by other influence nodes. This node is similar to the mask_influence, but generates the mask values using a simulation property instead of the distance to geometry. This is frequently very useful. For example one could modulate a gravity_influence using the aero property `voxel_fog_density`. Thi...

Simulation::Influence::radial_influence.summary: The radial influence applies an acceleration toward or away from a specified point. This also includes dropoff of effect with distance to that point, which will also affect any other influence nodes connected to this.

Simulation::Influence::set_influence_dra.summary: This influence property can be used to simulate effects of air drag. By its self the drag damps the simulation velocity. If there is also a force property for this influence then this will damp motion towards that accelleration, rather than zero velocity. This can simulate high drag in situations where the medium, like water, is flowing.

Simulation::Influence::set_influence_for.summary: This allows one to apply an acceleration to the simulation. By default it is like gravity, but if combined with drag it is like a wind force. One can connect vectorFields, such as a `fractal_turbulence_field` to control the direction of force over space. To use this node, plug its output into the `influences` input of a simulate node like `simulate_aero`, `simulate_particles`, or `simulate_mpm`.

Simulation::Influence::set_influence_kil.summary: This can be used to kill particles or smoke. To avoid killing everything one would typically connect it to a mask influence, and/or connect a scalarField to the kill value.

Simulation::Influence::set_influence_mas.summary: This controls the overall weight of the influence. If this is zero the influence will have no effect, while if the value is 1.0 the influence will have full effect. Mask values internally are clamped to be between zero and one. This needs to be connected to other influence nodes like set_influence_force to have a noticable effect. Typically one would connect a scalar field to the mask input, wh...

Simulation::Influence::turbulence_influe.summary: The turbulence influence applies a curl noise acceleration, which is useful for effects like air turbulence. A nice feature of the curl noise is that the resulting velocities are incompressible, like an air flow, which results in more natural particle smoke simulations. In such cases higher drag values will help the particles to more closely follow the curl noise flow instead of building up vel...

Simulation::Influence::vdb_influence.summary: The VDB influence applies a velocity from a VDB file to the simulation velocity. For high `drag` values with a `force_scale` of 1.0 the simulation will exactly follow the VDB velocity.

Simulation::Influence::volume_influence.summary: The volume influence applies the `voxel_velocity` property from a volume object as acceleration. This can be used to push particles using the velocity from an aero simulation. When doing that it helps to make the `force_scale` 1.0 and additionally connect to the `influence` port a drag_influence that has high drag. In this way the particles will exactly follow the flow from the aero simulation.

Simulation::Influence::vorticity_influen.summary: This applies vorticity confinement to the velocities of an simulation.  This helps encourage small scale vortices in the simulation that might get otherwise damped. It will make the simulation appear more turbulent and less viscous.This node only works with `simulate_aero` currently.

Simulation::Influence::wind_influence.summary: The wind influence simulates a simple wind of constant direction.

Simulation::Internal::memory_frame_cache.summary: This compound contains the port feedback mechanism that the `memory_cache` and `memory_file_cache` nodes utilize.  This building block for memory caching contains logic that determines whether the current frame of a Bifrost object passed into the node should be saved to memory inside of the feedback container. Simulation::Liquids::Internal::apply_gra.summary: This node applies gravity to the voxel-velocity field as well as to the point-velocities of the droplets.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::apply_sur.summary: This node applies a surface tension force to the voxel-velocity field.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::coarsen_r.summary: This compound coarsens and refines a liquid level set volume based on proximity to the liquid surface and colliders.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::compute_a.summary: This node computes the air-liquid distance property. If there are no colliders, the air-liquid distance is the same as the liquid surface level set. In the presence of colliders, the air-liquid distance measures the (negative) distance to the air-liquid interface at any point inside the liquid.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::compute_c.summary: The `compute_churn` node calculates the churn which refers to the angular speed tangential to the surface of the level set.

The `compute_collider_velocity` node computes the velocity of the input `colliders` by resampling at `time` +  `time_step` and adds it as a property named `voxel_collider_velocity`.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::compute_d.summary: The `compute_droplet` node updates the droplet property on the liquid and handles the transition of points between the droplet and fluid states.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::compute_m.summary: This node computes the maximum extrusion depth of an ocean surface mesh for a simulation guided by spectral ocean waves.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::compute_s.summary: This node computes the sources volumes from a set of input spectral ocean wave sources. Sources that are already voxelized are passed through.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::compute_v.summary: The `compute_vorticity` node calculates the accumulation of rotation magnitude (curl of velocity field) within voxels. When used in `liquid` the vorticity is transported with the flow.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::correct_a.summary: This node corrects the air-liquid distance property in the presence of colliders.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::count_poi.summary: The `count_points_per_voxel` adds a property named `voxel_point_count` to the input `liquid` which is the number of points inside each voxel.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::create_li.summary: This node creates a liquid object.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::emit_liqu.summary: This node refines the volume and emits liquid points into a liquid object.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::emit_poin.summary: The `emit_points` node emits points into the input liquid `object`.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::erase_poi.summary: The `erase_points` node erases points in the input liquid `object` based on input volumes that specify where to respectively retain and/or erase points.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::erode_liq.summary: This node locally erodes the liquid surface to better capture gravity surface waves, avoid artificial stiction to colliders and ensure hydrostatics with curved colliders. The erosion is based on various criteria. If the liquid is deep we always erode. If the liquid is shallow we erode fully if the local orientation of the solid is within the range allowed by the `normalized_erosion_angle_near_c...

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::flip_voxe.summary: The `flip_voxel_to_points` node transfers voxel properties to corresponding point properties in the input `liquid` object. A FLIP transfer interpolates the difference between the currect and previous value, while a PIC transfer interpolates the current value. Commonly the FLIP and PIC values will be blended together to transfer the property.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::guide_poi.summary: The `guide_points` node guides points outside of a simulation region in a guided simulation.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::interpola.summary: The `interpolate_passthrough_properties` node performs temporal interpolation of passthrough point properties from the `sources` to `out_liquid`.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::liquid_bo.summary: This node computes the minimum and maximum bounds of a liquid.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::mark_wave.summary: This node marks the faces in the `wave_bottom` and `wave_top` in the output per-face array `faces_to_delete` that should be deleted prior to extrusion of the

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::points_to.summary: This node computes a level set from the input liquid points and locally erodes the level set to better capture gravity surface waves, avoid artificial stiction to colliders and ensure hydrostatics with curved colliders. The erosion is based on various criteria. If the liquid is deep we always erode. If the liquid is shallow we erode fully if the local orientation of the solid is within the rang...
The `points_to_voxel` node transfers point properties to corresponding voxel properties in the input `liquid` object.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::project_v.summary: This node computes the pressure in the liquid and uses this to perform an orthogonal projection of the liquid velocity such that it is divergence free and hence conserves volume.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::reseed_po.summary: The `reseed_points` node reseeds points into the input liquid `object` to retain the user-specified point distribution. The liquid interior is defined by the `voxel_signed_distance` property.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::retile_po.summary: This node spatially re-tiles points into the tiles of the volume structure. This means that every point will be stored in the tile that its point position maps to.

Simulation::Liquids::Internal::transport.summary: This node transports points in a voxel-velocity field.

Simulation::Liquids::assign_guided_liqui.summary: This node assigns a matte to the input `liquid_geometry` and `collider_geometry` to facilitate combining the renders of these geometries with other elements in a compositing application.

Simulation::Liquids::basic_guided_liquid.summary: The `basic_guided_liquid_graph` sets up a simple guided liquid graph with node default values tailored for guided liquids. Add this node at the top level of a graph, explode it, and connect its inputs and outputs.

Simulation::Liquids::basic_liquid_graph.summary: The `basic_liquid_graph` sets up a simple graph that produces a liquid. Add this node at the top level of a graph, explode it, and connect its inputs and outputs.

Simulation::Liquids::blend_guided_liquid.summary: This node blends a guided liquid with a guide volume near and outside the simulation region.

Simulation::Liquids::create_ocean_surfac.summary: This compound creates an ocean surface mesh by displacing a mesh plane with an input set of waves. Additionally, simulation regions can be input to cut holes in the displaced mesh for use as a shell collider for foam simulation or for rendering.

Simulation::Liquids::dampen_guide_veloci.summary: The `dampen_guide_velocity_influence` can be used in conjunction with guided simulations to dampen spikes in velocity near the edges of the simulation regions where the simulated liquid layer becomes very thin.

Simulation::Liquids::get_points_from_til.summary: The `get_points_from_tile_tree` node gets all the properties in a volume targeting the `point_voxel_tile_tree` that match `property_expression` and converts them to a `points` geometry.

Simulation::Liquids::guided_liquid_alpha.summary: This node creates an alpha field for blending between a guided liquid and a guide volume near and outside the simulation region. The alpha field is zero in the liquid and one in the guide volume.

Simulation::Liquids::guided_liquid_setti.summary: This node exposes the settings for guided liquid simulations. The `guided_settings` output should be connected to the `additional_settings` input on the `liquid_solver_settings` node.

Simulation::Liquids::liquid_guide_spectr.summary: This node combines an array of input spectral waves from the `create_spectral_waves` node with properties that determine how the waves should be voxelized in the liquid solver. The output `geometry` should be passed to the `geometry` port of the `source_liquid` node.

Simulation::Liquids::liquid_guide_waves.summary: This node combines input arrays of dynamic and spectral waves with properties that determine how the waves should be voxelized in the liquid solver. The output `geometry` should be passed to the `geometry` port of the `source_liquid` node.

Simulation::Liquids::liquid_scope.summary: Displays diagnostics for the `liquid` output of `simulate_liquid`

Simulation::Liquids::liquid_solver_setti.summary: Sets options for liquid simulations. The output of this node should be connected to the `settings` input of a `simulate_liquid` node.

Simulation::Liquids::liquid_surface_tens.summary: Sets surface tension options for liquid simulations. The output of this node should be connected to the `additional_settings` input of a `liquid_solver_settings` node.

Simulation::Liquids::mesh_and_blend_liqu.summary: This node converts liquid points to a mesh and blends with a guide volume near and outside the simulation regions.

Simulation::Liquids::simulate_guided_rip.summary: The `simulate_guided_ripples` compound simulates secondary ripple effects for guided liquid simulations that originate outside of the simulation regions where liquid impacts the guide surface. The output `wave` can be used to displace both the liquid surface mesh as well as the surrounding guide ocean using the `displace_by_wave` compound.

Simulation::Liquids::simulate_liquid.summary: The `simulate_liquid` compound contains the core solver for liquid.

Simulation::Liquids::simulate_particle_f.summary: This node simulates a foam particles for an input liquid. To use this node, plug the output of a liquid simulation into the `liquid` input. The liquid object must have the properties `voxel_signed_distance` and `voxel_velocity`. It may also optionally have a `voxel_signed_collider_distance` property to be used for collisions and features like `max_solid_depth`. Due to adaptivity this collider d...

Simulation::Liquids::simulation_region.summary: Simulation regions define the volume inside which guided simulations take place.

Simulation::Liquids::source_liquid.summary: Specifies the parameters of a source that emits properties into the liquid simulation.

Simulation::MPM::constrain_mpm.summary: Use this compound to create constraints on the `point_position` of the source geometry that will be enforced during simulation. A constraint is a way to force certain points to travel according to the animated motion of either the input `mpm_source` geometry or the `constraint_geometry`. The position that a point is constrained to is called the target position. The constraint can either be hard...

Simulation::MPM::make_mpm_shell.summary: Specifies where `simulate_mpm` should create a thin shell of material. The main difference between the thin shell and the cloth model is that the shell model supports resistance to bending.  This is done by defining the curvature from the curvature of the limit Catmull-Clark subdivision surface.

Simulation::MPM::mpm_settings_to_scatter.summary: Calculates the density of points for `scatter_points` based on `mpm_solver_settings`. This is useful when you want to animate some properties of the particles with `passthrough_points` and `passthrough_properties`.

Simulation::MPM::mpm_snow_scope.summary: Visualizes the internal properties of snow particles output by `simulate_mpm`.

Simulation::MPM::mpm_solver_settings.summary: The `settings` output from this compound should be connected to the `settings` input of `simulate_mpm`.

Simulation::MPM::simulate_mpm.summary: The main compound for the Material Point Method (MPM) in Bifrost. You can use it to simulate a wide variety of physical materials including sand, snow, fluid, cloth, and fibers.

Simulation::MPM::source_mpm_fluid.summary: Specifies where `simulate_mpm` should create fluid particles should be created or sourced. This can be used to create a continuous stream of fluid, or a region of fluid.

Simulation::MPM::source_mpm_gel.summary: Specifies where `simulate_mpm` should create gel particles should be created or sourced. This can be used to create a continuous stream of gel, or a region of gel.

Simulation::MPM::source_mpm_rubber.summary: Specifies where to create rubber particles. Despite its name, `source_mpm_rubber` can be used for more than just rubber but any material where purely elastic behaviour is expected. The `rubber_source` output from this compound should be connected to the `sources` input of `simulate_mpm`.

Simulation::MPM::source_mpm_sand.summary: Specifies where `simulate_mpm` should create sand particles should be created or sourced. This can be used to create a continuous stream of sand, or a region of sand.

Simulation::MPM::source_mpm_snow.summary: Use to show `simulate_mpm` where snow particles should be created or sourced. This can be used to create a continuous stream of snow, or a region of snow. Despite its name `source_mpm_snow` can be used for more than just snow but other granular materials as well. This uses a more complicated model than `source_mpm_sand`, the major difference being that `source_mpm_snow` allows the snow to pack...

Simulation::MPM::split_points_by_materia.summary: Splits the `granular_particles` output into individual point clouds, one per material, including `fluid_particles`, `gel_particles`, `other_particles`, `rubber_particles`, `sand_particles`, and `snow_particles`.

Simulation::Nucleus::nucleus_collide_poi.summary: This node collides particles with an array of collision objects using the Maya Nucleus Solver.

Simulation::Nucleus::nucleus_points_to_m.summary: This node converts a `point_object` to a `out_mesh`.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::compute_dyn.summary: This node computes layers of dynamic wave displacement and velocity in depth below the surface.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::compute_spe.summary: This node computes layers of spectral wave displacement or velocity in depth below the surface.
This node voxelizes the velocity from a spectral wave image with depth layers into a volume.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::dilate_mask.summary: To define a mask for wave generation/collision, where 1.0 represents the interior of the generator and 0.0 represents the background. Keep the outlines fairly crisp.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::dynamic_wav.summary: Sets up a dynamic wave solver with `patch_size_x` by  `patch_size_z`, with resolution  `resolution_x` by  `resolution_z`.
Resets the dynamic_wave to the initial start value.
Sets a depth level array for the dynamic_wave.
Sets a drift velocity map for the dynamic_wave.
Sets a source map for the dynamic_wave.
Solves the dynamic_wave forward a time step.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::get_dynamic.summary: Gets the per-pixel array of the output wave simulation property representing the bottom depth.
Gets the per-pixel array of the output wave simulation drift velocity property.
Gets the per-pixel arrays of output wave simulation properties, including `slope`, `velocity`, as well as `displacement` and its derivatives (`displacement_derivatives`).

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::get_image_s.summary: Gets the `width` and `height` pixel count of the passed-in image.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::get_spectra.summary: Gets the per pixel arrays of output wave simulation properties, including `slope`, `velocity`, as well as `displacement` and its derivatives (`displacement_derivatives`).

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::offset_imag.summary: This node offset an image, in pixels based on the resolution of the image.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::sample_imag.summary: This node samples an image at a number of uv positions.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::sample_spec.summary: Samples the spectral wave at the input positions.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::smooth_imag.summary: Smooths an image using a Gaussian filter.

Simulation::Ocean::Internal::spectral_wa.summary: Sets up a spectral wave solver.
Updates the spectral wave to the current time.

Simulation::Ocean::basic_dynamic_wave_gr.summary: This is a simple graph showing a setup of a dynamic and spectral waves with foam. To use it first explode the graph, then connect to a terminal or output. The spectral waves on the plane geometry should then appear. One can then connect an object to the source_dynamic_wave node to create a wake into the water. A wake will be generated as the object moves.

Simulation::Ocean::compute_spectral_ocea.summary: This node computes an ocean volume based on an input array of spectral wave images that can be used as input for guided liquid simulations. It also adds a property named `displacement_high` to the `out_wave` ocean wave image which can be used to displace the output of the guided liquid simulation to add additional high frequency details. The input wave images will typically be the output of `cr...

Simulation::Ocean::compute_wave_volume.summary: This node computes an ocean volume based on an input array of dynamic and spectral wave images that can be used as input for guided liquid simulations. It also adds a property named `displacement_high` to the `out_wave` ocean wave image which can be used to displace the output of the guided liquid simulation to add additional high frequency details. The input wave images will typically be the o...

Simulation::Ocean::create_geo_wave_map.summary: This node lets one turn a source geometry into a wave_map to use with a dynamic wave simulation. It computes a 2D pixel map with bounds in XZ that can be connected to source inputs on a simulate_dynamics_waves node, such as height_source or obstruction. This map based on where the geometry is below the water height.

Simulation::Ocean::create_spectral_waves.summary: This computes a spectral wave simulation on a 2D grid and outputs it in a 2D wave object that may be used to displace geometry or as inputs to other simulations, like foam. The extent of the 2D simulation is defined by the bounds properties. Outside these bounds it seamlessly repeats if `periodic` is enabled.

Simulation::Ocean::create_wave_map.summary: This lets one define a 2d pixel map to use a source input for a dynamic wave simulation. This map is in XZ and projected down Y, and includes bounds in ZX. It can be uses for things like wake generation, wave obstruction, and water depth maps.

Simulation::Ocean::displace_by_wave.summary: This displaces an input geometry using an input array of wave objects. These are typically the outputs of create_spectral_waves or simulate_dynamic_wave nodes. The different input waves displacements are sampled at the geometry point positions and sum together for the final displacement.

Simulation::Ocean::displace_by_wave_high.summary: This displaces an input geometry using an input array of wave objects. These are typically the outputs of `create_spectral_waves` or `simulate_dynamic_wave` nodes and passed through the `split_image_into_low_high_frequencies` node. The different input waves displacements are sampled at the geometry point positions and summed together for the final displacement. The `displace_by_wave_high_freque...

Simulation::Ocean::dynamic_wave_settings.summary: This contains all the global settings used by the `simulate_dynamic_waves node`. The extent of the 2D simulation is defined by the bounds properties. Outside these bounds it repeats if `periodic` is enabled.

Simulation::Ocean::sample_wave_data.summary: This can be used to sample a wave simulation and compute properties for a passed in array of positions. Note that some outputs are only available if either `output_slope`, `horizontal_displacement` or `output_velocity` is enabled on the wave solver. In particular `output_slope` and `horizontal_displacement` must both be enabled to access anything other than `displacement` and `velocity`.

Simulation::Ocean::sample_wave_property.summary: This can be used to sample a wave simulation output for a passed in array of positions.

Simulation::Ocean::scale_wave_height.summary: This allows one to scale the displacement values for a wave object. It may be especially useful when modifying cached wave values.

Simulation::Ocean::simulate_dynamic_wave.summary: This computes a dynamic wave simulation on a 2D grid and outputs it in a 2D wave object that may be used to displace geometry or as inputs to other simulations, like foam. The extent of the 2D simulation is defined by the bounds properties on the settings. Outside these bounds it repeats if `periodic` is enabled.

Simulation::Ocean::simulate_foam.summary: This computes a dynamic foam on a 2D grid and outputs it in a 2D foam image object that may be used in rendering foam on an object. It inherits properties from the input wave, such as the bounds and whether it is periodic or not.

Simulation::Ocean::source_dynamic_wave.summary: This lets one turn a source geometry (like a boat) into height and obstruction maps to use for generating wakes in a dynamic_wave_simulation node. The output should be connected to the simulate_dynamic_waves `source`. Simulation::Ocean::split_image_into_low_.summary: This node splits an image property into low and high frequencies.

Simulation::Ocean::wave_set_foam.summary: This samples input foam simulations at the location of input geometry positions and sets a foam property on the geometry. The different input foams are summed together.

Simulation::Particles::basic_particles_g.summary: The `basic_particles_graph` sets up a simple default graph that will emits particles which fall under gravity and die after one second.

Simulation::Particles::filter_particles.summary: This compound is useful for secondary emission from one particle system into another. It allows one to remove points from a point object based on collide state or a specified point property along with a threshold.
